mapStates.name: Ahn'Qiraj and the opening adventuring age — interpretive state

mapStates.name: Southern empires and revolution — interpretive research map

mapStates.name: Kaldorei ascendance — interpretive research map

mapStates.name: Primordial Azeroth during the Black Empire — interpretive research map

mapStates.name: The first Long Vigil — interpretive early state

mapStates.name: Migrations and founding powers — interpretive middle state

mapStates.name: The Fourth War — interpretive global state
mapStates.interpretationNote: This state communicates a multi-theater faction war through broad narrative anchors. It does not assert precise fronts, territorial boundaries, or mission routes.

mapStates.name: The awakened Dragon Isles — interpretive state
mapStates.interpretationNote: The isles are an approximate narrative anchor on the original post-Cataclysm atlas; local coastlines and expedition routes are not reconstructed.

mapStates.name: Khaz Algar and The War Within — interpretive state
mapStates.interpretationNote: Khaz Algar's marker is approximate and compresses surface and subterranean theaters into one story focus; it is not a dungeon or zone map.

mapStates.name: Midnight announced horizon — evidence-boundary state

mapStates.name: N'Zoth's assaults — interpretive pressure state

mapStates.name: Shadowlands covenant relationships — interpretive field

mapStates.name: Ordered primordial Azeroth — interpretive research map
mapStates.interpretationNote: This after-state preserves the Era 1 research coastline so the historical change remains legible. mapStates.name: Draenor before the Horde — interpretive research state
mapStates.interpretationNote: This original world plate communicates an intact Draenor and broad coexistence of orc clans and draenei communities. Its coastline, ecology, influence areas, and story figures are reconstruction, not reproduced official cartography or exact borders.

mapStates.name: Draenor during the Horde's rise — interpretive research state
mapStates.cartographyLabel: INTERPRETIVE DRAENOR WAR AND CORRUPTION STATE
mapStates.interpretationNote: This state preserves intact Draenor while showing restrained environmental decline and broad campaign pressure. The routes are directional narrative reconstructions; no exact war front, clan border, or troop path is asserted.

mapStates.name: Azeroth during the First War — interpretive campaign state
mapStates.interpretationNote: The state uses an original post-Sundering reconstruction whose large-scale hierarchy emphasizes coherent western Kalimdor, eastern Eastern Kingdoms, and northern Northrend around the Great Sea. Campaign pressure remains broad rather than treating game missions as a surveyed campaign. The portal changes worldspace; it is not rendered as a geographic line between planets.

mapStates.name: Azeroth during the Second War — interpretive campaign state
mapStates.interpretationNote: This late state uses the same original continental reconstruction as the First War state, with coherent western Kalimdor, eastern Eastern Kingdoms, and northern Northrend clearly separated by ocean. It shows the Alliance coalition, the Horde's broad northern offensive, Blackrock, and the return to the Dark Portal. Its regions and routes are interpretive strategic summaries, not exact national borders, fleet tracks, or troop movements.

mapStates.name: Icecrown and the Frozen Throne — interpretive conclusion state
mapStates.interpretationNote: This state centers the race toward Icecrown and Arthas's ascent. Sites and routes are approximate strategic anchors on an original continental reconstruction, not reproduced game coordinates or mission paths.

mapStates.name: The Legion's return and Mount Hyjal — interpretive state
mapStates.interpretationNote: This state summarizes westward migration, corruption, and the convergence at Mount Hyjal through inferred routes and relational actor anchors. It does not reconstruct RTS missions or exact troop movements.

mapStates.name: The northern crisis and fall of Lordaeron — interpretive state
mapStates.interpretationNote: The plague, Arthas's northern pursuit, and the Scourge advance are shown as broad narrative pressure. No exact outbreak boundary, city footprint, or complete army route is asserted.

mapStates.name: Illidan's Outland campaign — interpretive episode state
mapStates.interpretationNote: Outland uses its own local atlas coordinate system. The episode records portal closures and the overthrow of Magtheridon without drawing a false spatial line back to Azeroth or copying game-zone cartography.

mapStates.name: The Legion invasion — interpretive campaign map
mapStates.interpretationNote: The scorched terrain and broad pressure area explain a continent-spanning invasion without asserting tactical front lines. Actor points are narrative anchors; the resistance convergence route is a simplified directional reading rather than a traced march.

mapStates.name: Zin-Azshari before the invasion — interpretive research map

mapStates.name: The sundered world — interpretive research map
mapStates.interpretationNote: This state communicates the irreversible breakup of primordial Kalimdor and the central oceanic wound. It is original, simplified cartography and does not claim exact ancient coastlines, island counts, survivor routes, or the surveyed position of every later continent.

eras.summary: Political choices around the Well enabled the Burning Legion's first invasion, drew defenders from across ancient Kalimdor, and ended with the Great Sundering.

entities.name: Adventurers of Azeroth
entities.shortDescription: A broad interpretive grouping for the independent champions and expeditionary bands who repeatedly entered the era's crises.
entities.body: This is a narrative category, not a single canonical organization. Its original ensemble image represents anonymous participants and does not assign one identity or allegiance to every adventurer.

entities.name: Aggramar
entities.shortDescription: The titan who discovered the imperiled world of Azeroth and urged the Pantheon to act through purpose-built servants rather than overwhelming force.
entities.body: Aggramar recognized both the promise of Azeroth's sleeping world-soul and the danger posed by the Black Empire. Blizzard's first-party account emphasizes his concern that the Pantheon's colossal intervention could destroy what they meant to save.

entities.name: Ahn'Qiraj
entities.shortDescription: The sealed southern stronghold opened during a cross-faction war effort against C'Thun's forces.

entities.name: Al'Akir
entities.shortDescription: The cunning Elemental Lord of air, whose forces relied on spying, division, and sudden storms.

entities.name: The Alliance of Lordaeron
entities.shortDescription: A coalition of human kingdoms and allied peoples formed in response to the Horde after Stormwind's fall.

entities.name: The Amani Empire
entities.shortDescription: The forest-troll power whose ancestral northern lands came into conflict with Quel'Thalas and later Arathor.
entities.body: This record presents the Amani as an organized people defending and contesting lands, not as anonymous obstacles in another kingdom's founding story. The influence area and generated group representation are interpretive.

entities.name: Aman’Thul
entities.shortDescription: The first titan to awaken in Chronicle's account, who crossed the Great Dark in search of others of his kind.
entities.body: Aman’Thul's search gathered the awakened titans into the Pantheon. When the Pantheon confronted the corruption on Azeroth, his direct removal of Y'Shaarj revealed how deeply the Old Gods had rooted themselves in the world.

entities.name: Anduin Lothar
entities.shortDescription: Stormwind's champion who led its survivors north and became supreme commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron.

entities.name: Aqir
entities.shortDescription: Resilient insectoid servants formed from the Old Gods' organic matter, first set to building the Black Empire and later drawn into a world-spanning war with the ancient troll powers.
entities.body: The atlas treats the aqir as a changing ancient people rather than a single timeless empire. The northern and southern successor societies that emerged from their retreat belong to later map states and should not be collapsed into one precise border.

entities.name: Arathor
entities.shortDescription: The first great human nation, united under Thoradin and centered at Strom.
entities.body: Arathor's atlas region is a broad political reading across a long era. The generated group image represents a coalition of early human communities rather than one uniform army or later kingdom culture.

entities.name: Archimonde
entities.shortDescription: A Burning Legion commander summoned into Azeroth who led the advance toward Nordrassil and was destroyed at Mount Hyjal.

entities.name: Argus
entities.shortDescription: The shattered world that served as the Burning Legion's seat of power and the final theater of this era's Legion campaign.

entities.name: Arthas Menethil
entities.shortDescription: A prince of Lordaeron whose pursuit of the plague led through Stratholme and Northrend, into the service of the Lich King, and ultimately to the Frozen Throne.
entities.body: The split-state portrait is an original interpretive device showing the era's transformation without claiming that both appearances occupied one instant.

entities.name: Azeroth's World-Soul
entities.shortDescription: A titan spirit developing within the young world's core, whose immense growth drew in much of Azeroth's Spirit.
entities.body: Chronicle presents the world-soul as the reason Azeroth's elementals lacked the balancing fifth element. This record describes the primordial account and does not resolve later perspectives on Azeroth's nature.

entities.name: Queen Azshara
entities.shortDescription: The exceptionally gifted and widely admired queen under whom the kaldorei empire reached extraordinary power before the War of the Ancients.
entities.body: Era 3 ends with Azshara's ascent and the concentration of power around her court. In Era 4, the research account follows her court's decision to admit the Burning Legion through the Well and her survival beneath the sea after the Sundering. The generated figure is an original interpretive portrait rather than licensed character art.

entities.name: The Black Empire
entities.shortDescription: The civilization of Old God domains, citadels, and temple cities that spread across primordial Azeroth.
entities.body: The shaded atlas extent communicates broad influence only. Chronicle supports world-spanning expansion but does not provide survey-grade borders, so every boundary shown here is explicitly inferred.

entities.name: Blackhand
entities.shortDescription: The visible first warchief of the Old Horde, elevated while the Shadow Council exercised concealed influence.

entities.name: Blackrock Spire
entities.shortDescription: The mountain stronghold near which the Second War's leadership and momentum changed decisively.

entities.name: The Broken Isles
entities.shortDescription: The island region at the center of the Burning Legion's renewed invasion of Azeroth.

entities.name: The Burning Legion
entities.shortDescription: The demonic army that entered ancient Kalimdor through the Highborne portal and devastated the kaldorei empire.
entities.body: The group image represents a vast and varied invasion force through a few readable silhouettes. It is intentionally not a claim about a particular formation, commander grouping, or battlefield coordinate.

entities.name: Cenarius
entities.shortDescription: An ancient guardian of the wilds and Malfurion's teacher who joined the defense of Kalimdor against the Legion.
entities.body: Cenarius stands for the living world's entrance into the war, not for a precisely mapped battlefield deployment. His generated figure is an original interpretive representation.

entities.name: The Class Orders
entities.shortDescription: Distinct orders of champions who organized against the Burning Legion when established armies were divided.
entities.body: The shared adventurer ensemble is an interpretive visual shorthand. The orders remained distinct communities rather than one permanent faction.

entities.name: The Cosmic Forces
entities.shortDescription: Chronicle's cosmology arranges reality through opposed forces: Light and Shadow, Life and Death, and Order and Disorder.
entities.body: The familiar cosmology chart is used as a subject index, not copied as artwork. Later accounts may qualify how complete or objective this arrangement is.

entities.name: The Dark Portal
entities.shortDescription: The constructed gateway that joined Draenor and Azeroth and made the First War a conflict between worlds.
entities.body: The atlas represents the portal as corresponding anchors in two local worldspaces. It is never drawn as an ordinary geographic line between their coordinate systems.

entities.name: The Dark Trolls
entities.shortDescription: A reclusive nocturnal troll people whose migration toward the Well of Eternity became the beginning of the kaldorei story.
entities.body: Chronicle places this community apart from the greater troll struggles. The atlas shows movement toward the Well as an interpretive transition, not as an exact migration route preserved by a contemporary record.

entities.name: Dath'Remar Sunstrider
entities.shortDescription: The Highborne leader associated with the exile from Kalimdor and the founding of Quel'Thalas.
entities.body: Dath'Remar is shown as a navigator-founder during the migration rather than through later royal iconography. The portrait is an original interpretive likeness and not licensed character art.

entities.name: The Draenei of Draenor
entities.shortDescription: The exiled people led by Velen who made a refuge on Draenor before Kil'jaeden turned the orcs against them.
entities.body: The preview centers their communities as inhabitants with their own history, not merely as an obstacle in the Horde's formation.

entities.name: Draenor
entities.shortDescription: The intact world inhabited by orc clans and draenei before its later destruction and transformation into Outland.
entities.body: This record represents Draenor during Era 6 only. Its atlas plate is an original reconstruction and does not reproduce official geography.

entities.name: The Dragon Isles
entities.shortDescription: The ancestral isles of dragonkind, awakened and returned to the world's history.

entities.name: The Dragon Soul
entities.shortDescription: An artifact empowered by the Dragon Aspects and then turned by Neltharion against their alliance during the war.
entities.body: The atlas uses the contemporary name Dragon Soul for the event. Its location is not asserted as a permanent point; the artifact is visually carried in Neltharion's contextual representation.

entities.name: The Dragonflights
entities.shortDescription: Azeroth's great dragonflights, recalled to the Dragon Isles and drawn into the age's renewed struggles.
entities.body: The five-dragon spiral is a symbolic original composition and does not identify a specific gathering, scale, or formation.

entities.name: Durotan
entities.shortDescription: Frostwolf chieftain who recognized the corruption surrounding the Horde and refused Mannoroth's blood for his clan.

entities.name: The Dwarven Clans
aliases: Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans
entities.shortDescription: The three great dwarven clans whose succession struggle divided Ironforge and reshaped Khaz Modan.
entities.body: The collective record keeps the related clans visible together before showing their political dispersal. Its generated figure uses three balanced delegations and is symbolic rather than a literal battlefield formation.

entities.name: The Earthen of Khaz Algar
entities.shortDescription: Titan-forged peoples whose long-isolated cultures are encountered beneath and across Khaz Algar.
entities.body: The original ensemble combines anonymous callings for map readability and is not a canonical gathering of named individuals.

entities.name: The Elemental Hosts
entities.shortDescription: The innumerable air, fire, earth, and water spirits led by Azeroth's four Elemental Lords.
entities.body: This collective editorial label groups the four rival elemental forces for battle playback. Chronicle describes them as separate hosts whose control of Azeroth shifted constantly, not as a permanent unified state.

entities.name: The Empire of Zul
entities.shortDescription: A coalition of ancient troll peoples assembled under Zandalari leadership when the awakened aqir threatened them across Kalimdor.
entities.body: The name describes the wartime union rather than a single permanent territorial state. Its member peoples retained distinct lands and identities, and the coalition loosened after the long pursuit of the aqir ended.

entities.name: Eversong Woods
entities.shortDescription: The blood elf homeland named in the announced premise for Midnight; no campaign outcome is asserted here.

entities.name: The Forge of Origination
entities.shortDescription: A southern titan-forged world-facility built to help stabilize Azeroth and retain a final re-origination safeguard against total corruption.
entities.body: The Forge worked in concert with the northern Forge of Wills. Its public overview states both its healing purpose and its terrible contingency without suggesting that the latter was used during this era.

entities.name: The Forsaken
entities.shortDescription: Free-willed undead who broke from the Lich King's control and established a foothold in fallen Lordaeron under Sylvanas.

entities.name: The Frozen Throne
entities.shortDescription: The prison and seat of the Lich King at Icecrown, reached by Arthas after his victory over Illidan.

entities.name: The Great Dark Beyond
entities.shortDescription: The physical universe of innumerable worlds and stars described in Chronicle's cosmological account.
entities.body: Its point on the cosmography is a reading aid only. A universe has not been reduced to a literal map marker.

entities.name: Grim Batol
entities.shortDescription: The northern mountain stronghold established by the Wildhammers after their expulsion from Ironforge.
entities.body: The point is approximate at atlas scale and belongs to the post-dispersal political state.

entities.name: Grom Hellscream
entities.shortDescription: An orc chieftain who fell again beneath Mannoroth's corruption and then died breaking the pit lord's hold over his people.

entities.name: Gul'dan
entities.shortDescription: Ner'zhul's apprentice, empowered by the Legion, who built the Shadow Council and deepened the Horde's dependence on fel power.

entities.name: The Highborne Exiles
entities.shortDescription: The arcane-practicing Highborne who left Kalimdor and eventually established a new homeland in the east.
entities.body: The record follows a migrating population across a long and incompletely measured journey. Its route is deliberately simplified, and the generated family-and-scholar group avoids presenting the migration as only a military expedition.

entities.name: The Highborne
entities.shortDescription: The privileged kaldorei arcanists around Azshara whose ritual at the Well opened the way for the Burning Legion.
entities.body: This dossier treats the court collectively so the tour can explain institutional choice without inventing a complete roster. The figure and its placement are original interpretive representations, not a palace plan or licensed art.

entities.name: The Defenders of Mount Hyjal
entities.shortDescription: A temporary coalition of night elves, Horde forces, Alliance survivors, and their leaders assembled against the Legion's advance.
entities.body: This grouping describes cooperation in one existential defense; it does not erase the distinct peoples, commands, or conflicts within it.

entities.name: The Second Well of Eternity
entities.shortDescription: The new arcane well created by Illidan upon Mount Hyjal after the Sundering.
entities.body: This record distinguishes the Hyjal well from the destroyed central Well of ancient Kalimdor. Its marker is approximate within the atlas interpretation of Mount Hyjal and should not be read as surveyed terrain.

entities.name: Icecrown
entities.shortDescription: The northern region containing the Frozen Throne and the final contest between Arthas and Illidan in this era.

entities.name: Illidan's Outland Coalition
entities.shortDescription: The temporary coalition through which Illidan, Kael'thas, Lady Vashj, and their forces closed portals and seized power in Outland.
entities.body: The atlas treats this as an era-specific military coalition, not a timeless or internally uniform polity.

entities.name: Illidan Stormrage
entities.shortDescription: A gifted kaldorei sorcerer whose dangerous choices and knowledge of the Legion became part of the struggle at the Well.
entities.body: This research record stays within the war itself and does not import Illidan's later appearance or identity into the ancient map. The portrait therefore omits the signs of his later demonic transformation.

entities.name: The Iron Horde
entities.shortDescription: A war machine formed on an alternate Draenor that opened an invasion route toward Azeroth.
entities.body: The ensemble art is an original anonymous representation of the Iron Horde's industrial military character, not a reconstruction of named commanders.

entities.name: Ironforge
entities.shortDescription: The mountain city contested by the three dwarven clans during their succession war.
entities.body: The world-scale point locates the mountain-city tradition approximately; no internal city plan or exact ancient perimeter is asserted.

entities.name: Jaina Proudmoore
entities.shortDescription: A mage who investigated the plague, rejected Arthas's course at Stratholme, led survivors west, and joined the defense of Mount Hyjal.

entities.name: The Kaldorei Empire
entities.shortDescription: The civilization that arose around the Well of Eternity, mastered its arcane energies, and expanded swiftly across ancient Kalimdor.
entities.body: Its rise changed the political balance inherited from the trolls and southern empires. The broad influence shown by the atlas is a research visualization, not a claim that ancient rule followed a precise modern-style frontier.

entities.name: Kang
entities.shortDescription: The pandaren teacher associated with the unarmed discipline that helped turn resistance to the mogu into a wider revolution.
entities.body: Kang's importance lies not in a single mapped duel but in a method that could spread among a disarmed people. The figure is therefore placed relationally beside the southern uprising rather than assigned an exact battlefield.

entities.name: The Keepers
entities.shortDescription: The greatest titan-forged, empowered by members of the Pantheon to command the war and safeguard the ordering of Azeroth.
entities.body: The keepers led the armies that broke the Black Empire, contained the remaining Old Gods, stabilized the world-wound, established Ulduar, and directed the works that reshaped Azeroth. Individual duties are summarized here without turning the guided era into separate biographies.

entities.name: Kel'Thuzad
entities.shortDescription: A necromancer and Scourge agent whose plague cult helped prepare Lordaeron for destruction and the Legion's return.

entities.name: Khaz Algar
entities.shortDescription: The island and subterranean regions at the opening of The War Within.

entities.name: Kil'jaeden
entities.shortDescription: A Burning Legion lord whose pursuit of Velen's exiles drove the manipulation of Draenor's orcs.

entities.name: The Kingdom of Stormwind
entities.shortDescription: The southern human kingdom that faced the first invasion through the Dark Portal and fell at the end of the First War.

entities.name: Lei Shen
entities.shortDescription: The first mogu emperor, who united rival kings and established a far-reaching imperial order in the southern lands.
entities.body: Lei Shen's rise gave the divided mogu a new unity of purpose and brought other peoples under their rule. This portrait is an original interpretive visualization and does not claim an exact historical appearance.

entities.name: Light and Shadow
entities.shortDescription: Opposed primordial powers at the beginning of Chronicle's account of the Warcraft cosmos.
entities.body: This record keeps Chronicle Volume 1's creation account distinct from later cosmological perspectives. It does not claim that the diagram gives either power a physical location.

entities.name: The Kaldorei of the Long Vigil
entities.shortDescription: The post-Sundering night-elven society that guarded Kalimdor and watched for the Legion's return.
entities.body: This collective record represents a long-lived society containing priestly, sentinel, druidic, and other responsibilities; it does not reduce ten thousand years to one permanent army. The generated group image is symbolic and interpretive.

entities.name: Lordaeron
entities.shortDescription: The northern human kingdom around which the wartime Alliance formed, later broken by the Scourge during the Third War.

entities.name: The Maelstrom
entities.shortDescription: The immense oceanic vortex left at the center of the world after the Well collapsed and the continents broke apart.
entities.body: The post-Sundering terrain makes the central wound unmistakable. Its geometry is an interpretive atlas focus, not an exact ancient survey or a claim that the modern coastline appeared fully formed in one instant.

entities.name: Malfurion Stormrage
entities.shortDescription: A young druid whose bond with the natural world became central to opposing the Legion and closing the way through the Well.
entities.body: The tour follows Malfurion's strategic role without collapsing the resistance into a single hero. His generated portrait is an original interpretive likeness for this ancient period.

entities.name: Mannoroth
entities.shortDescription: A pit lord whose blood bound much of the forming Horde more tightly to the Burning Legion's design.

entities.name: Medivh
entities.shortDescription: The Guardian of Tirisfal whose corruption and contact with Gul'dan enabled the Dark Portal and the invasion of Azeroth.

entities.name: The Mogu Empire
entities.shortDescription: The southern empire forged by Lei Shen from divided mogu kingdoms and expanded through the conquest and subjugation of neighboring peoples.
entities.body: This dossier distinguishes Lei Shen's imperial project from the earlier keeper-directed role of the mogu. Its map extent is interpretive and deliberately avoids a hard frontier unsupported by the research sources.

entities.name: Mount Hyjal
entities.shortDescription: The mountain refuge reached by many survivors after the Sundering and a threshold into the Long Vigil.
entities.body: Era 4 ends at arrival and refuge. The second Well, Nordrassil, and the institutions of the Long Vigil belong to Era 5 so that consequences are not narrated before their own sourced slice.

entities.name: Neltharion the Earth-Warder
entities.shortDescription: The Dragon Aspect who turned the newly forged Dragon Soul against the allies gathered to defend Azeroth.
entities.body: Later ages know him by another name, but this record uses his identity at the time of the betrayal. The figure and disk are interpretive representations; they do not reproduce licensed creature or artifact designs.

entities.name: Neptulon
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of water, portrayed as a patient strategist who struck divided rivals.

entities.name: Ner'zhul
entities.shortDescription: A respected orc shaman whom Kil'jaeden deceived into directing the clans against the draenei before he rejected the Legion's course.

entities.name: The New Horde
entities.shortDescription: The community Thrall gathered from liberated orcs and new allies, distinguished from the Old Horde by its changing purpose and future in Kalimdor.

entities.name: The Night Elf Resistance
entities.shortDescription: Kaldorei defenders and allied peoples who opposed Azshara's court and the Burning Legion during the War of the Ancients.
entities.body: The coalition changed as the war widened. This collective record avoids presenting one leader or one body of troops as the whole resistance; the generated group figure is a symbolic, accessible overview.

entities.name: Nordrassil
entities.shortDescription: The World Tree planted over the second Well of Eternity on Mount Hyjal.
entities.body: Nordrassil marks the postwar answer to the danger beneath Hyjal and the beginning of a very different kaldorei order. The tree is represented by its terrain focus and accessible label rather than a generic troop marker.

entities.name: Northrend
entities.shortDescription: The northern continent from which the Lich King's power threatened the living.

entities.name: N'raqi
entities.shortDescription: Intelligent servants formed from the Old Gods' organic matter and used as taskmasters within the expanding empire.

entities.name: The Old Gods
entities.shortDescription: Void-linked entities that struck Azeroth, spread corruption through the world, and drove tendrils toward its core.
entities.body: The Era 1 account treats the Old Gods collectively except where Chronicle specifically identifies Y'Shaarj. Later sources name and distinguish additional Old Gods; those records should be introduced only with their own citations.

entities.name: The Old Horde
entities.shortDescription: The militarized coalition of orc clans formed on Draenor and sent through the Dark Portal into Azeroth.
entities.body: This era-specific name distinguishes the first Horde from later political communities that inherited, rejected, or transformed its memory.

entities.name: The Orc Clans of Draenor
entities.shortDescription: Independent orc communities whose ancestral and shamanic traditions preceded their coercive consolidation into the Old Horde.
entities.body: The collective record keeps the clans visible as distinct peoples before political and demonic manipulation gathered many of them into a war machine.

entities.name: Orgrim Doomhammer
entities.shortDescription: The orc warrior who killed Blackhand, exposed the Shadow Council, and led the Horde through the later First War and the Second War.

entities.name: Outland
entities.shortDescription: The shattered remnants of Draenor, treated as a separate worldspace rather than a distant region of Azeroth.

entities.name: The Ancient Pandaren
entities.shortDescription: One of the peoples subjected by the mogu empire and central to the uprising that ended its rule.
entities.body: The public summary stays at the level supported by the current research packet: a people denied weapons and written learning who developed other means of preserving discipline and resisting imperial rule.

entities.name: Pandaria
entities.shortDescription: A long-hidden land drawn into renewed faction conflict and the consequences of that conflict.

entities.name: The Pantheon of Order
entities.shortDescription: A company of awakened titans who traveled the Great Dark, ordering worlds and seeking more world-souls.
entities.body: After discovering Azeroth's threatened world-soul, the Pantheon intervened against the Black Empire, empowered the keepers, and left the ordered world in their care.

entities.name: Primordial Kalimdor
entities.shortDescription: The largest continent of primordial Azeroth, shown here with an interpretive rather than surveyed outline.
entities.body: The source supports a single great continental setting and describes Y'Shaarj's civilization near its center. The exact coastline in this atlas is a reconstruction and must not be read as a measured canonical boundary.

entities.name: Quel'Thalas
entities.shortDescription: The high-elven kingdom founded in the northern Eastern Kingdoms around the Sunwell.
entities.body: The political region is intentionally broad and changes meaning across the founding and later-kingdom map states. It does not claim a surveyed ancient border or erase the Amani relationship to the same lands.

entities.name: Ragnaros
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of fire, characterized by direct, destructive force against his rivals.

entities.name: Sargeras
entities.shortDescription: The distant master of the Burning Legion whom Azshara's Highborne sought to bring bodily into Azeroth through the Well.
entities.body: Sargeras does not arrive on the physical map in this era. His contextual figure represents the will and intended destination of the portal ritual, and its placement is relational rather than geographic.

entities.name: The Scourge
entities.shortDescription: The undead host and plague apparatus serving the Lich King, used to break the northern kingdoms and prepare the Legion's return.

entities.name: The Seven Human Kingdoms
entities.shortDescription: The sovereign human states that emerged from Arathor's long political fragmentation.
entities.body: This aggregate record preserves the atlas-scale transition from one empire to several states without pretending that all seven separated on one date or shared one culture. Individual kingdom dossiers belong to later era production where they become causal actors.

entities.name: The Shadow Council
entities.shortDescription: Gul'dan's concealed circle of warlocks and agents, created to steer the Horde behind its visible warchief.

entities.name: The Shadowlands Covenants
entities.shortDescription: The distinct powers encountered across the realms of the Shadowlands during the struggle beyond the broken veil.
entities.body: The four anonymous envoys are symbolic, interpretive representations of distinct covenant traditions; their placement communicates relationship rather than geography.

entities.name: The Realms of the Shadowlands
entities.shortDescription: Afterlife realms presented here as a relational field, not a measured geographic continent.

entities.name: Shattrath
entities.shortDescription: The principal draenei city on Draenor, devastated during the Horde's campaign against the draenei.

entities.name: Stormwind City
entities.shortDescription: The capital attacked and destroyed at the close of the First War before its later reconstruction.

entities.name: Stratholme
entities.shortDescription: A Lordaeron city whose infected population became the center of Arthas's catastrophic decision to purge it.

entities.name: Strom
entities.shortDescription: The fortified center of Arathor and the seat associated with Thoradin's unified nation.
entities.body: The atlas point is approximate at world scale and supports the political narrative rather than reconstructing an exact ancient city footprint.

entities.name: The Sunwell
entities.shortDescription: The arcane fount created by the high elves at a convergence of ley energies in their new homeland.
entities.body: The atlas treats the Sunwell as a founding center in Era 5 and carries its later corruption only in the separate Third War state.

entities.name: Sylvanas Windrunner
entities.shortDescription: The ranger-general who resisted the Scourge at Quel'Thalas, was raised into undeath, and later led free-willed undead in Lordaeron.
entities.body: The split-state portrait communicates a transformation across time and is explicitly interpretive rather than a literal simultaneous appearance.

entities.name: Thaurissan
entities.shortDescription: The Dark Iron city established in the Redridge Mountains after the clan's expulsion from Ironforge.
entities.body: This is the pre-volcanic city associated with the War of the Three Hammers, not a dossier for the later Blackrock Depths capital. Its point is approximate at world scale.

entities.name: Therazane
entities.shortDescription: The Elemental Lord of earth, protective of her children and defended by formidable mountain barriers.

entities.name: King Thoradin
entities.shortDescription: The human warlord who united tribes into Arathor and played a central role in the Troll Wars.
entities.body: Thoradin's generated portrait is a restrained original interpretation of an early coalition-builder, not a reconstruction of a licensed artifact illustration or later human heraldry.

entities.name: Thrall
entities.shortDescription: The orc leader who liberated interned orcs, formed a new Horde, crossed to Kalimdor, and joined the defense of Mount Hyjal.

entities.name: The Titan-forged
entities.shortDescription: Armies and workers of living stone and metal created to defeat the Black Empire, protect Azeroth, and help shape the wounded world.
entities.body: The first hosts fought beneath empowered keepers. Later titan-forged peoples undertook different labors across Azeroth, from raising mountains and tending machinery to carving waterways and guarding the keepers' works.

entities.name: Turalyon
entities.shortDescription: An Alliance paladin who rallied the army after Lothar's death and helped drive the Horde back to the Dark Portal.

entities.name: The Twisting Nether
entities.shortDescription: A volatile astral realm formed from energies released around the creation of the physical universe.
entities.body: Chronicle describes the Nether as interwoven with the Great Dark Beyond while remaining distinct from it. The atlas uses no geographic distance between the two.

entities.name: Tyrande Whisperwind
entities.shortDescription: A priestess of Elune who fought with and sustained the resistance during the War of the Ancients.
entities.body: Tyrande's role is presented as spiritual leadership joined to active defense. Her generated portrait is an original interpretive likeness, not licensed character art.

entities.name: Ulduar
entities.shortDescription: The keepers' great northern stronghold and the seat of the Forge of Wills during the ordering of Azeroth.
entities.body: Ulduar anchored the keepers' work in the far north of ancient Kalimdor. Its atlas marker is a broad reconstruction from that regional description, not a surveyed primordial coordinate.

entities.name: The Void Lords
entities.shortDescription: Shadow-aligned beings who sought to corrupt a world-soul but could not directly manifest their full power in the physical universe.
entities.body: Chronicle presents the Old Gods as instruments of this design. The record does not map the Void Lords to a physical territory.

entities.name: The Well of Eternity
entities.shortDescription: The immense arcane lake formed when the keepers stabilized the wound left by Y'Shaarj's removal.
entities.body: The Well was Azeroth's exposed lifeblood brought into balance by wards. It nourished life, empowered kaldorei civilization, became the gateway contested during the War of the Ancients, and collapsed in the catastrophe remembered as the Great Sundering.

entities.name: World-Souls
entities.shortDescription: Mysterious titan spirits that can form within some worlds and awaken after ages of growth.
entities.body: The record describes Chronicle Volume 1's titan account. It does not assert that every world contains such a soul.

entities.name: Xal'atath
entities.shortDescription: A Void-aligned power whose designs frame the opening movement of the Worldsoul Saga.
entities.body: The figure is an original interpretive portrait. This record stops at the announced Midnight premise and asserts no unreleased outcome.

entities.name: Y'Shaarj's Central Bastion
entities.shortDescription: An editorial label for the greatest Black Empire bastion, built around Y'Shaarj near the center of Azeroth's largest continent.
entities.body: Chronicle does not provide a proper name or exact coordinates for this bastion. The atlas marker is approximate and exists to communicate the source's near-the-center relationship, not a canonical point location.

entities.name: Y'Shaarj
entities.shortDescription: The Old God identified by Chronicle as the greatest of the group, surrounded by the Black Empire's largest bastion.

entities.name: Zin-Azshari
entities.shortDescription: Azshara's capital at the shores of the Well of Eternity and the center of the Highborne portal ritual.
entities.body: The atlas places the capital only as an approximate focus beside the interpretive Well. It does not reconstruct streets, palace limits, or the full historical shoreline.

entities.name: Ancient Zuldazar
entities.shortDescription: The highland center of the Zandalar tribe and a political heart of the earliest troll civilization represented in this era.
entities.body: Its placement on primordial Kalimdor is shown only as an inferred regional focus. The research map does not claim a surveyed ancient coastline, city footprint, or political boundary.

events.name: The War Effort Opens Ahn'Qiraj

date.label: Early in the age of adventurers

events.summary: Alliance and Horde communities supplied a shared war effort before champions entered Ahn'Qiraj to confront C'Thun's forces.
events.description: The record preserves the unusual scale of cooperation without reconstructing server-specific contributions or raid tactics.

events.name: The Alliance of Lordaeron Forms

date.label: After Stormwind's fall and before the Second War

events.summary: Stormwind's warning and the approaching Horde threat drew human kingdoms and allied peoples into a military coalition centered on Lordaeron.

events.name: The Allied Powers Defeat the Amani

date.label: At the conclusion of the Troll Wars

events.summary: The combined high-elven and human campaign broke the immediate Amani offensive and sharply reduced the empire's regional power without ending the Amani people.

events.name: Awakening of Aman’Thul

date.label: After worlds formed within the Great Dark

events.summary: Aman’Thul awoke from the world that had nurtured his spirit and began searching the cosmos for other nascent titans.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: The Aqir Awaken

date.label: After the early troll powers had spread

events.summary: Ancient aqir forces emerged again and pressed into troll-held lands, turning scattered rivalry into a shared existential danger.

events.name: The Aqir Successor Powers Emerge

date.label: After the long troll pursuit

events.summary: Separated aqir populations entrenched themselves in distant refuges, producing new northern and southern powers rather than restoring one united dominion.

events.name: Arathor Fragments into the Seven Kingdoms

date.label: By approximately 1,200 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Over generations, Arathor's distant city-states became sovereign powers and the unified human empire gave way to seven kingdoms.

events.name: Archimonde Is Destroyed at Mount Hyjal

date.label: At the climax of the Third War

events.summary: The defenders delayed Archimonde until Malfurion released Nordrassil's gathered power, destroying the Legion commander and repelling the assault.

events.name: Archimonde Is Summoned into Azeroth

date.label: After the northern kingdoms are broken

events.summary: The Scourge's campaign opened the way for Archimonde and the Burning Legion to return and turn their advance toward Kalimdor and Nordrassil.

events.name: The Campaign Reaches Argus

date.label: At the culmination of the Legion campaign

events.summary: A direct link carried the coalition to shattered Argus and the Burning Legion's seat of power.

events.name: Arthas Ascends the Frozen Throne

date.label: At the close of the Frozen Throne campaign

events.summary: After defeating Illidan, Arthas reached the Frozen Throne and joined with the Lich King, establishing the new order that closes this era.

events.name: Arthas Claims Frostmourne

date.label: During Arthas's Northrend pursuit

events.summary: Arthas pursued the Scourge into Northrend and took up Frostmourne, a choice that bound his fate more tightly to the Lich King.

events.name: Azeroth Is Ordered

date.label: After the world-forges were established

events.summary: The titan-forged raised mountains, opened waterways, dredged seas, maintained great works, and helped make the wounded world stable enough for life to flourish.

events.name: Azshara Rises to the Throne

date.label: Near the height of prewar kaldorei power

events.summary: Azshara became queen of a powerful kaldorei civilization whose court and arcane ambitions stood at the threshold of the next catastrophe.

events.name: Black Empire Dominion

date.label: After the elemental resistance failed

events.summary: The elementals failed to dislodge the Old Gods and were enslaved; without that resistance, Black Empire influence extended over much of the world.

events.name: Rise of the Black Empire

date.label: After the Old Gods' arrival

events.summary: The n'raqi directed the aqir in building citadels and temple cities around the Old Gods; Y'Shaarj's central bastion became the greatest of these domains as their holdings spread.

events.name: The Legion's Crusade Is Broken

date.label: At the end of the Argus campaign

events.summary: The Argus campaign broke the Burning Legion's immediate cosmic crusade, closing the era with victory and a wounded world left behind.

events.name: The Class Orders Rise Against the Legion

date.label: During the Legion's return

events.summary: As the Burning Legion invaded through the Broken Isles, distinct class orders organized champions for a common defense.

events.name: The Dark Portal Opens

date.label: The opening of the Dark Portal

events.summary: Gul'dan and the corrupted Guardian Medivh completed a gateway between Draenor and Azeroth, allowing the Horde to cross between worlds.

events.name: The Dark Trolls Settle Near the Well

date.label: Beginning around 15,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: A reclusive dark troll people moved toward the center of Kalimdor and made their home near the Well of Eternity.

events.name: Deathwing Shatters the World

date.label: The Cataclysm

events.summary: Deathwing's return caused the Cataclysm, violently reshaping regions across Azeroth and forcing a world-spanning defense.

events.name: The Dragon Isles Awaken

date.label: After the return from the Shadowlands

events.summary: The Dragon Isles awakened, calling the dragonflights home and opening a new expedition into their ancient inheritance.

events.name: The Dwarven Succession Crisis Opens

date.label: Approximately 230 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: The death of Ironforge's high king broke a tense balance among the Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron clans and opened a war for the mountain city.

events.name: The Early Troll Powers Rise

date.label: About 16,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: Troll peoples flourished across the forests and jungles of ordered Kalimdor, with the Zandalar, Amani, Gurubashi, and Drakkari among the powers that took shape.

events.name: The First War Begins

date.label: After the Dark Portal opens

events.summary: Horde forces entered Azeroth and began the war against the Kingdom of Stormwind.

events.name: The Forsaken Emerge in Lordaeron

date.label: As the Lich King's control weakens after the Legion's defeat

events.summary: Sylvanas and other undead broke from the Lich King's control and established a new, precarious power in the ruins of Lordaeron.

events.name: The Fourth War Campaign Ends

date.label: At the close of the Fourth War campaign

events.summary: A rebellion joined with Alliance pressure against Sylvanas's rule, bringing the war campaign to its end without erasing its losses.

events.name: The Fourth War Erupts

date.label: After the Legion campaign

events.summary: Alliance and Horde entered a global war of footholds, reprisals, and deepening fractures after the Legion's defeat.

events.name: The Great Sundering

date.label: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

events.summary: The Well's destruction tore primordial Kalimdor apart, drowned great reaches of land, and left the Maelstrom at the center of a new ocean.

events.name: Grom Breaks Mannoroth's Bond

date.label: During the Kalimdor campaign

events.summary: After falling again beneath Mannoroth's corruption, Grom joined Thrall against the pit lord and died in the act that broke the immediate demonic bond over their people.

events.name: Gul'dan Abandons the Second War

date.label: During the Horde's northern campaign

events.summary: Gul'dan withdrew forces from the Horde's campaign for his own expedition, weakening Orgrim's offensive at a critical time.

events.name: Gul'dan Forms the Shadow Council

date.label: During the political consolidation of the clans

events.summary: After Ner'zhul resisted the Legion's course, Gul'dan organized a concealed warlock council and tightened hidden control around the forming Horde.

events.name: The Highborne Are Exiled

date.label: Approximately 7,300 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Conflict over arcane practice ended with a Highborne population leaving Kalimdor under Dath'Remar's leadership.

events.name: The Highborne Open the Way

date.label: At the opening of the War of the Ancients

events.summary: Azshara's favored Highborne used the Well to establish a portal through which the Burning Legion could enter Azeroth.

events.name: The Horde Is Defeated and the Dark Portal Is Destroyed

date.label: At the end of the Second War; working chronology

events.summary: The Alliance drove the Horde back to the gateway, destroyed the original Dark Portal, and captured many of the defeated orcs.

events.name: The Defenders of Hyjal Unite

date.label: Before Archimonde reaches Nordrassil

events.summary: Night elves, the New Horde, and Alliance survivors accepted a temporary common defense as the Legion advanced toward Mount Hyjal.

events.name: Illidan Assaults the Frozen Throne

date.label: After Kil'jaeden commands Illidan to destroy the Frozen Throne

events.summary: Illidan returned from Outland and drove toward Icecrown, but Arthas defeated him before reaching the Frozen Throne.

events.name: Illidan Creates a Second Well

date.label: In the immediate aftermath of the Sundering

events.summary: Illidan used preserved water from the original Well to create a new arcane well upon Mount Hyjal and was imprisoned after the act was discovered.

events.name: Illidan Seizes Power in Outland

date.label: After the Battle of Mount Hyjal

events.summary: Illidan and his allies closed portals, defeated Magtheridon's rule, and established a new center of power in Outland.

events.name: The Iron Horde Opens an Alternate Front

date.label: After the Siege of Orgrimmar

events.summary: An invasion from an alternate Draenor opened a separate-world campaign against the Iron Horde.

events.name: The Kaldorei Ascend

date.label: Across generations beside the Well

events.summary: Changed by long proximity to the Well, the emerging kaldorei mastered arcane power, built cities, and expanded across Kalimdor.

events.name: Kil'jaeden Finds the Draenei on Draenor

date.label: Approximately thirteen years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Kil'jaeden discovered Velen's exiles on Draenor and chose the orc clans as the instrument of his revenge.

events.name: The Burning Legion Enters Azeroth

date.label: After the Highborne portal opened

events.summary: Demonic forces poured through the portal at Zin-Azshari and began destroying the empire whose court had admitted them.

events.name: Lei Shen Unites the Mogu

date.label: During the age of divided southern kingdoms

events.summary: Lei Shen overcame rival mogu kings and gathered their competing realms into a single imperial power.

events.name: The Lich King Falls at Icecrown

date.label: During the Northrend campaign

events.summary: The campaign through Northrend reached Icecrown, where Arthas's reign as the Lich King ended.

events.name: The Long Vigil Begins

date.label: After Nordrassil was established

events.summary: Post-Sundering kaldorei society took up a long watch over Kalimdor and against the return of the Burning Legion.

events.name: Lordaeron Falls to the Scourge

date.label: After Arthas returns from Northrend

events.summary: Arthas returned as a death knight, killed his father, and helped bring the kingdom of Lordaeron under the Scourge.

events.name: Anduin Lothar Falls Near Blackrock Spire

date.label: During the Alliance counteroffensive in the Second War

events.summary: Lothar died during the confrontation near Blackrock Spire, creating a moment of shock that Turalyon turned into resolve.

events.name: Midnight Stands at the Archive's Horizon

date.label: Announced future chapter at the archive cutoff

events.summary: The announced Midnight premise turns toward Xal'atath's assault on the blood elf homelands; its outcome remains outside this archive's evidence boundary.
events.description: This is an announced-premise record, not a completed historical outcome. Eversong, Zul'Aman, Harandar, and the Voidstorm are named only to the extent supported by the pre-release overview.

events.name: The Mogu Empire Expands

date.label: After Lei Shen's unification

events.summary: The new empire subdued neighboring peoples and imposed its rule across much of the southern lands later known as Pandaria.

events.name: Neltharion Turns the Dragon Soul on His Allies

date.label: During the War of the Ancients

events.summary: After using the Dragon Soul against the Legion, Neltharion revealed his betrayal and shattered the unity of the dragonflights.

events.name: Ner'zhul Is Deceived Against the Draenei

date.label: Before Gul'dan assumes the Legion's work

events.summary: Kil'jaeden exploited Ner'zhul's authority and grief to turn orc suspicion and violence toward the draenei.

events.name: The New Horde Crosses to Kalimdor

date.label: As the northern crisis widens

events.summary: Warned of the coming danger, Thrall led the New Horde west across the sea and began building a future in Kalimdor.

events.name: Resistance Forms Against the Invasion

date.label: As the Legion spread beyond Zin-Azshari

events.summary: Kaldorei who rejected Azshara's course organized a resistance in which Malfurion, Tyrande, and Illidan each played consequential roles.

events.name: Nordrassil Is Planted

date.label: After the second Well was discovered

events.summary: A World Tree was planted over the new Well at Hyjal, binding the postwar refuge to a new charge of protection.

events.name: The Assault of N'Zoth Is Defeated

date.label: At the end of the N'Zoth campaign

events.summary: Champions carried the struggle into Ny'alotha and ended N'Zoth's immediate assault on Azeroth.

events.name: N'Zoth Is Unleashed

date.label: After the Fourth War campaign

events.summary: N'Zoth's release brought assaults and corrupting visions against an already wounded Azeroth.

events.name: Arrival of the Old Gods

date.label: After untold ages of elemental conflict

events.summary: A group of Old Gods struck Azeroth from the Great Dark, embedded themselves in different parts of the world, and extended their influence toward its core.

events.name: The Old Gods Are Contained

date.label: After the fall of the Black Empire

events.summary: Unable to remove the remaining Old Gods without repeating the wound caused by Y'Shaarj's destruction, the keepers bound them in prisons beneath Azeroth.

events.name: Scattering of the Old Gods

date.label: Before the Old Gods struck Azeroth

events.summary: The Void Lords made the Old Gods and cast them through the Great Dark, hoping that some would find and corrupt a world-soul.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label. The cosmography asserts sequence and purpose but no origin coordinate, route, or measurable number of Old Gods.

events.name: Orc Clans Drink Mannoroth's Blood

date.label: Before the final assault on Shattrath

events.summary: Many orc leaders accepted Mannoroth's blood and its power, binding the Horde more deeply to the Legion; Durotan kept the Frostwolves from drinking.

events.name: Orgrim Doomhammer Becomes Warchief

date.label: During the First War

events.summary: Orgrim killed Blackhand, broke much of the Shadow Council's concealed power, and assumed leadership of the Horde.

events.name: The Dark Portal Leads Back to Outland

date.label: After the Ahn'Qiraj campaign

events.summary: A renewed passage through the Dark Portal carried Azeroth's forces into shattered Outland and the conflicts rooted there.

events.name: The Pandaren Revolution

date.label: After generations of mogu rule

events.summary: Resistance associated with Kang spread among the mogu's subject peoples until the imperial order broke and the southern lands entered a new age.

events.name: Pandaria Returns to the Wider World

date.label: After the Cataclysm

events.summary: The long-hidden land of Pandaria became a theater of exploration and intensifying Alliance–Horde conflict.

events.name: The Pantheon Departs

date.label: After the ordering of Azeroth

events.summary: With Azeroth stabilized and its guardians appointed, the Pantheon departed while the keepers and titan-forged remained to watch over the world.

events.name: The Pantheon Discovers Azeroth

date.label: During the Black Empire's dominion

events.summary: Aggramar discovered Azeroth's nascent titan and the Old Gods rooted around it, bringing the imperiled world to the Pantheon's attention.

events.name: Gathering of the Pantheon

date.label: During Aman’Thul's search for other titans

events.summary: The awakened titans found one another, formed the Pantheon, and traveled onward to order worlds and seek more of their kind.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the Pantheon's formation in Chronicle Volume 1.

events.name: Emergence of the Physical Universe

date.label: At the beginning of Chronicle's cosmic account

events.summary: The conflict between primordial Light and Void gave rise to the physical universe, while released energies formed the Twisting Nether.
events.description: The event name is an editorial label for the creation sequence described in Chronicle Volume 1; it is not presented as a formally named Warcraft event.

events.name: The Plague Spreads Through Lordaeron

date.label: At the opening of the Third War

events.summary: A mysterious plague spread through Lordaeron as the Cult of the Damned and Scourge prepared the kingdom's destruction.

events.name: The Portal at the Well Collapses

date.label: At the end of the War of the Ancients

events.summary: The defenders disrupted the Legion's gateway before Sargeras could enter, and the unstable Well collapsed around the broken portal.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Are Founded

date.label: Approximately 6,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: The exiles established Quel'Thalas in the northern Eastern Kingdoms and created the Sunwell as the heart of their new civilization.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and the Sunwell Fall

date.label: During the Scourge advance after Lordaeron's fall

events.summary: The Scourge broke Quel'Thalas, raised Sylvanas into undeath, and corrupted the Sunwell while advancing its larger design.

events.name: Quel'Thalas and Arathor Form a Wartime Alliance

date.label: During the Troll Wars

events.summary: Facing an overwhelming Amani assault, Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor and shared limited arcane instruction in exchange for military aid.

events.name: Ragnaros Re-emerges at Blackrock

date.label: At the end of the War of the Three Hammers

events.summary: A desperate Dark Iron summoning brought Ragnaros back into the world, devastated the southern mountains, and ended the dwarven war beneath a new volcanic power.

events.name: The Second War Begins

date.label: After the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron

events.summary: The Horde drove north while the newly formed Alliance organized a defense across several kingdoms and theaters.

events.name: The Covenant Campaigns Converge

date.label: During the Shadowlands campaign

events.summary: Champions worked among distinct covenant realms whose campaigns formed the broad framework of resistance in the afterlife.

events.name: Shattrath Falls to the Horde

date.label: Near the culmination of the Horde's war against the draenei

events.summary: The Horde's assault devastated Shattrath and broke the principal center of organized draenei resistance, though draenei survivors endured.

events.name: The Siege Ends Garrosh's Rule

date.label: At the end of the Pandaria conflict

events.summary: Opposition from within and beyond the Horde converged on Orgrimmar and ended Garrosh Hellscream's rule.

events.name: The Primordial Imbalance

date.label: Before the arrival of the Old Gods

events.summary: As Azeroth's world-soul developed, it consumed much of the fifth element, Spirit, leaving the native elementals without its balancing influence.
events.description: This descriptive event record captures Chronicle's causal explanation for the violent state of primordial Azeroth's elementals.

events.name: Stormwind Falls

date.label: At the end of the First War

events.summary: The Horde captured and devastated Stormwind, forcing surviving leaders and refugees to flee north.

events.name: Stratholme Is Purged

date.label: After the plague is discovered in Lordaeron

events.summary: Convinced Stratholme's people were infected, Arthas ordered the city purged; Jaina and Uther rejected the course, deepening his isolation.

events.name: Survivors Reach Mount Hyjal

date.label: Immediately after the Great Sundering

events.summary: Many surviving defenders reached the lands around Mount Hyjal, carrying the memory of the lost world into the beginning of the Long Vigil.

events.name: Thoradin Unites Arathor

date.label: Approximately 2,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

events.summary: Thoradin brought scattered human tribes beneath one banner and established Arathor around the fortified center of Strom.

events.name: Thrall Liberates Interned Orcs

date.label: Nearly thirteen years after the Horde's defeat

events.summary: Thrall freed orcs from internment and gathered a new Horde whose purpose was not identical to the conquered Old Horde.

events.name: The Titan-forged Are Mustered

date.label: After direct intervention wounded Azeroth

events.summary: The Pantheon created armies of stone and metal and empowered the greatest among them as keepers to lead the war for Azeroth.

events.name: Turalyon Rallies the Alliance

date.label: Immediately after Lothar's death

events.summary: Turalyon rallied the shaken Alliance and sustained the counteroffensive that drove the Horde south.

events.name: The Veil into the Shadowlands Is Shattered

date.label: At the opening of the Shadowlands crisis

events.summary: Sylvanas shattered the veil between life and death, drawing champions into the Shadowlands and its covenant realms.

events.name: The War Within Opens in Khaz Algar

date.label: Opening chapter of the Worldsoul Saga

events.summary: Xal'atath's gathering threat led champions into Khaz Algar and its subterranean worlds, where the Earthen became central allies and witnesses.

events.name: The World-wound Is Stabilized

date.label: After the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned

events.summary: The keepers raised wards around Azeroth's bleeding wound until its arcane energies settled into the Well of Eternity.

events.name: Ancient Allies Join the Defense

date.label: During the widening War of the Ancients

events.summary: Cenarius and other powers of ancient Kalimdor joined the defense, while the Dragon Aspects prepared a weapon intended to drive back the Legion.

events.name: The World-forges Are Established

date.label: During the healing of Azeroth

events.summary: The keepers established complementary facilities in the far north and south to stabilize Azeroth and sustain the work of ordering it.

events.name: The Removal of Y'Shaarj

date.label: At the beginning of the Pantheon's intervention

events.summary: Aman’Thul tore Y'Shaarj from Azeroth, destroying the Old God but opening a terrible wound in the sleeping world-soul.

battles.name: The Battle of Mount Hyjal

date.label: At the culmination of the Third War

battles.summary: A temporary coalition delayed Archimonde's advance long enough for Malfurion to call upon Nordrassil's power and destroy him.
battles.description: This dossier treats Mount Hyjal as an era-defining strategic defense. Its phases explain convergence, delay, and outcome without replaying Warcraft III missions or asserting exact camps and troop paths.

objectives.summary: Reach Nordrassil and seize the power gathered at Mount Hyjal.
Delay the Legion's advance and preserve the mountain long enough for a final answer.

phases.title: The Legion turns toward the mountain
phases.summary: Archimonde drives the invasion toward Mount Hyjal and Nordrassil.
phases.narration: The northern kingdoms had already paid the price of the Scourge's design. In Kalimdor, the Legion now bent its strength toward the crown of the mountain and the power rooted there.

phases.title: Old enemies accept one defense
phases.summary: Night elves, New Horde forces, and Alliance survivors converge under a temporary common purpose.
phases.narration: No single people could hold the road alone. Those who had met as strangers and rivals gathered beneath one necessity, retaining their own names even as they took their places in a shared defense.

phases.title: The ascent is made costly
phases.summary: The defenders yield ground while buying the time on which the mountain's survival depends.
phases.narration: This was not a clean wall drawn across the land. It was delay purchased in stages, positions abandoned only after time had been wrested from the invader and carried upward toward Nordrassil.

phases.title: Archimonde reaches for Nordrassil
phases.summary: The Legion commander reaches the World Tree as Malfurion's final response gathers.
phases.narration: Archimonde climbed within reach of the ancient tree. The long defense had not barred every step; it had created the moment in which another kind of strength could answer him.

phases.title: The tree's gathered power is released
phases.summary: Malfurion calls upon Nordrassil's power; Archimonde is destroyed and the invasion is broken.
phases.narration: At the last height, Malfurion called upon the power gathered around Nordrassil. Archimonde was destroyed. Victory did not restore the kingdoms already fallen, but it broke the Legion's assault and left the survivors to shape what came after.

outcome.summary: The coalition delayed the advance until Nordrassil's released power destroyed Archimonde, ending the Legion's immediate invasion while leaving the northern kingdoms transformed.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Mount Hyjal and Nordrassil are broadly located, but the conflict comprised several defensive positions whose exact mission geography is not asserted here.

battles.name: The Elemental Assault on the Black Empire

date.label: After the Black Empire began to spread

battles.summary: For the first time, Azeroth's rival elemental hosts united against the Old Gods and attacked the Black Empire's growing cities.
battles.description: This descriptive title groups a broad conflict rather than asserting one localized battle. Chronicle describes firestorms and stone barriers striking Black Empire cities but does not provide mappable routes.

objectives.summary: Remove the Old Gods and their growing civilization from Azeroth.
Preserve and expand the Old Gods' domains through n'raqi and aqir forces.

phases.title: Rivals unite
phases.summary: The four elemental powers recognized a common threat.
phases.narration: As the Black Empire widened its shadow, the ancient enemies understood at last that none could stand alone. For the first time, Azeroth's elemental powers gathered against one foe.

phases.title: Firestorms cross the empire
phases.summary: Air and fire combined against Black Empire cities.
phases.narration: Wind and flame went forth together. Al'Akir's tempests bore the wrath of Ragnaros across the dark dominion, and immense firestorms descended upon the empire's citadels.

phases.title: Stone closes around the cities
phases.summary: Therazane raised barriers against the empire's settlements.
phases.narration: Then Therazane laid her strength upon the field. Jagged walls rose at her bidding, hemming in the servants of the Old Gods and breaking against their temple cities.

phases.title: The servant hosts endure
phases.summary: The empire answered through the n'raqi and aqir.
phases.narration: Yet from the cities came the n'raqi and the innumerable aqir. Rank after rank endured the elemental fury, until even the joined hosts could not overcome them.

phases.title: The resistance fails
phases.summary: The Old Gods defeated and enslaved the Elemental Lords.
phases.narration: In the end the resistance was broken. The Old Gods bound the Elemental Lords, and with no native power left to bar its way, the Black Empire spread across much of the world.

outcome.summary: The elemental resistance failed; the Elemental Lords were enslaved and the Black Empire extended its dominion over much of Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The conflict covered multiple unnamed sites. No exact marker or route is asserted.

battles.name: The Elemental Wars

date.label: Untold ages before the Old Gods' arrival

battles.summary: The four Elemental Lords and their hosts fought across primordial Azeroth for ages, with dominion shifting continually and no lasting victor.
battles.description: The title is a descriptive grouping for Chronicle's world-spanning elemental conflict. Because the source supplies no stable front or exact battlefield, the atlas records its geography as unknown.

objectives.summary: Each rival elemental host sought dominion and the remaking of the world in its own image.

phases.title: The winds divide
phases.summary: Al'Akir weakened rivals through spies, deception, and sudden storms.
phases.narration: From the high airs Al'Akir watched the wars below. Through spies and deception he divided his enemies, and his tempests fell only when rival strength had already been spent.

phases.title: Fire overwhelms
phases.summary: Ragnaros answered strategy with volcanic, direct destruction.
phases.narration: Ragnaros placed no faith in subtle designs. Before him volcanoes opened, fire crowned the land, and ash followed where his overwhelming host had passed.

phases.title: Earth endures
phases.summary: Therazane sheltered behind mountains and counterattacked exhausted enemies.
phases.narration: Therazane gathered her children behind the strength of mountains. There they endured the fury of their foes, and only when the assault was weary did the earth rise to answer.

phases.title: Water divides and conquers
phases.summary: Neptulon waited for rival armies to separate before crushing them.
phases.narration: Neptulon did not squander his waters against a gathered host. He waited until the armies of his foes were divided, then loosed the deep against them in their weakness.

outcome.summary: No permanent victor emerged; control shifted while the conflict continued for untold ages.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning conflict without exact battle sites or stable fronts, so no marker or route is drawn.

battles.name: The First War

date.label: From the opening of the Dark Portal through the fall of Stormwind

battles.summary: A multi-year invasion in which the Old Horde crossed from Draenor, fought the Kingdom of Stormwind, changed leadership, and ultimately captured the southern capital.
battles.description: This dossier presents an atlas-scale strategic sequence. The source chapter supports repeated offensives, political upheaval, and Stormwind's fall, but not one exact battlefield or a complete surveyed route assembled from game missions.

objectives.summary: Establish the invasion on Azeroth and break the Kingdom of Stormwind.
Contain the invaders, preserve the kingdom, and uncover the power enabling the portal.

phases.title: A new enemy crosses the threshold
phases.summary: Horde forces emerge from the Dark Portal and begin probing the southern kingdom.
phases.narration: The first crossings did not reveal the full weight waiting beyond the gate. They were enough to turn a hidden act of sorcery into war and to teach Stormwind that the enemy had no homeland upon its maps.

phases.title: Stormwind survives the first blows
phases.summary: The defenders resist early attacks while the Horde learns the land and gathers greater strength.
phases.narration: The kingdom did not fall at the first alarm. Resistance bought time, but each return carried greater confidence, while fear and uncertainty divided those who still believed the war could be contained.

phases.title: The hand behind the gate is uncovered
phases.summary: Stormwind's defenders discover Medivh's role, severing the Azeroth-side will that had enabled the invasion.
phases.narration: The road of the invasion led inward as well as east. The Guardian who should have watched the world had helped open it, and stopping him ended one design without recalling the armies already across the threshold.

phases.title: The Horde changes masters
phases.summary: Orgrim kills Blackhand, attacks the Shadow Council's power, and assumes command.
phases.narration: The invaders' unity concealed another war. Orgrim struck down Blackhand and tore at the council behind him. The Horde changed masters, yet its armies remained upon Azeroth and its hunger for victory did not depart with the old warchief.

phases.title: The southern kingdom is broken
phases.summary: The Horde captures Stormwind and surviving leaders carry warning north.
phases.narration: At last the southern walls failed. Victory gave the Horde a ruined capital, while the sea carried survivors and a warning toward kingdoms that had not yet understood that Stormwind's war would soon become their own.

outcome.summary: Stormwind was captured and devastated, the First War ended in Horde victory, and survivors escaped north to seek a wider alliance.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The First War comprised many movements and engagements. No single exact battlefield point is asserted; the displayed route is explicitly inferred.

battles.name: The Fourth War Campaign

date.label: After the Legion's defeat

battles.summary: A strategic dossier of the faction war's widening fronts, internal rebellion, and political conclusion.
battles.description: The dossier avoids reproducing mission routes or reducing a global war to one precise marker.

phases.title: The war spreads through distant footholds
phases.summary: Both factions establish campaigns across new fronts.
phases.narration: The wounded world received another war, its ships and armies carrying old mistrust into lands already rich with histories of their own.

phases.title: Each victory enlarges the debt
phases.summary: The conflict's reprisals and campaigns deepen its human and political cost.
phases.narration: Territory changed hands; grief did not. Every answered wound became an argument for the next.

phases.title: The Horde fractures around its leadership
phases.summary: Opposition to Sylvanas grows within the Horde.
phases.narration: Within the Horde, loyalty to a people and obedience to a ruler no longer pointed along the same road.

phases.title: Opposition converges
phases.summary: Horde rebels and Alliance pressure align against Sylvanas's rule.
phases.narration: Those who had stood on opposite sides of the war arrived at one gate with purposes that overlapped, though their losses did not become one story.

phases.title: The campaign ends; its consequences remain
phases.summary: Sylvanas departs and the Fourth War campaign closes.
phases.narration: The banners lowered before the memories beneath them. An ending to the campaign was not an undoing of what the campaign had made.

outcome.summary: The rebellion and Alliance pressure ended Sylvanas's rule and closed the Fourth War campaign.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The Fourth War spanned many theaters and is not assigned a false single battlefield.

battles.name: The Frozen Throne Campaign

date.label: After the Battle of Mount Hyjal

battles.summary: A cross-world sequence in which Illidan established power in Outland, returned to strike Icecrown, and lost the final race to Arthas.
battles.description: The dossier links Outland and Icecrown through deterministic map-state changes. Each world keeps local coordinates, and no false geographic route is drawn between them.

objectives.summary: Build the strength to assault Icecrown and destroy the Frozen Throne.
Reach and preserve the Frozen Throne before Illidan's coalition can break it.

phases.title: Illidan turns exile into a campaign
phases.summary: Illidan and his allies close portals within Outland and challenge its existing ruler.
phases.narration: Beyond Azeroth, Illidan made refuge into preparation. His coalition moved through a broken world, closing the roads by which greater powers might follow and gathering strength beneath an alien sky.

phases.title: A new power rises in Outland
phases.summary: The coalition overthrows Magtheridon's rule and establishes a base for the next command.
phases.narration: The shattered world did not become whole beneath new masters. Yet its balance changed. Illidan stood at the center of a coalition held together by need, ambition, and the enemies waiting beyond it.

phases.title: The contest returns to Azeroth
phases.summary: Illidan's forces and Arthas move toward Icecrown from different purposes and paths.
phases.narration: The next road cannot be drawn across the void between worlds. The atlas therefore changes states: Outland recedes, Icecrown rises, and two purposes narrow toward the same throne.

phases.title: The last passage is contested
phases.summary: Illidan reaches Icecrown but Arthas defeats him before the Frozen Throne.
phases.narration: At Icecrown the broad campaign became a final contest. Illidan's assault failed before the throne could be destroyed, and the way above remained open to Arthas.

phases.title: Arthas climbs into a new order
phases.summary: Arthas reaches the Frozen Throne and becomes the Lich King.
phases.narration: Arthas climbed the last height and took the Frozen Throne's power into himself. The prince who had ridden out to save a kingdom now presided over the force that had destroyed it, and a darker inheritance passed into the coming age.

outcome.summary: Illidan's assault failed; Arthas reached the Frozen Throne and became the Lich King, establishing a new power inherited by the Age of Adventurers.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The campaign spans separate worldspaces and broad theaters. Only local inferred routes are shown, never a line between Outland and Azeroth.

battles.name: The Icecrown Citadel Campaign

date.label: At the culmination of the Northrend campaign

battles.summary: A broad strategic dossier tracing the coalition's advance through Icecrown to the fall of Arthas as the Lich King.
battles.description: These phases summarize campaign logic rather than raid encounters or exact troop movements.

objectives.summary: Preserve the Lich King's dominion from Icecrown.
Break the Scourge's northern power and confront the Lich King.

phases.title: The war reaches Northrend
phases.summary: Coalition forces establish the long campaign's northern front.
