phases.narration: Across the cold sea, armies and wandering companies entered a land already shaped by the throne above it.

phases.title: The Scourge yields no easy road
phases.summary: The campaign crosses a continent of entrenched undead power.
phases.narration: Every road northward bore the memory of older defeats, and every victory narrowed the distance to their author.

phases.title: Icecrown Citadel is breached
phases.summary: The assault enters the seat of the Lich King's rule.
phases.narration: At the glacier's crown, the campaign passed from a war across land into a reckoning within the citadel itself.

phases.title: The throne receives its challengers
phases.summary: Champions confront Arthas at the center of his power.
phases.narration: The lost prince stood where an age before he had claimed the crown; those who climbed to him carried the cost of all the years between.

phases.title: Arthas's reign ends
phases.summary: The Lich King's immediate reign is broken, though Northrend's burden is not made simple.
phases.narration: The king fell. The ice did not forget him, and victory did not turn the dead back into the living, but the long command from Icecrown was ended.

outcome.summary: Arthas was defeated at Icecrown and his reign as the Lich King ended.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Icecrown is broadly placed; dossier phases do not assert exact landings, formations, or encounter positions.

battles.name: The Second War

date.label: After Stormwind's fall through the destruction of the original Dark Portal

battles.summary: A multi-theater war in which the Horde drove north against the Alliance of Lordaeron before internal fracture and an Alliance counteroffensive reversed the campaign.
battles.description: The dossier describes strategic direction and leadership changes rather than replaying missions or simulating units. Land, sea, and aerial theaters are condensed into two explicitly inferred atlas routes.

objectives.summary: Break the northern coalition and secure lasting Horde dominion on Azeroth.
Stop the northern offensive, liberate occupied lands, and close the gateway that sustains the invasion.

phases.title: The Horde drives north
phases.summary: Orgrim leads a broad offensive from the conquered south toward the Alliance kingdoms.
phases.narration: Stormwind's fall had opened the road but not ended resistance. The Horde drove north across many theaters, while a coalition still new to itself learned to answer as more than seven separate fears.

phases.title: The coalition becomes an army
phases.summary: Lothar coordinates the Alliance while its members defend several threatened realms.
phases.narration: Alliance was first a promise spoken under approaching danger. Campaign made it practice. Different peoples, commanders, and interests held together because none could afford the loneliness in which Stormwind had fallen.

phases.title: The northern kingdoms face the invasion
phases.summary: The Horde campaign threatens the Alliance heartlands but does not secure a final victory.
phases.narration: The war reached lands that had once heard Stormwind's ruin as distant news. Yet breadth became a burden as well as strength: every new front lengthened the purpose holding the Horde together.

phases.title: Ambition divides the offensive
phases.summary: Gul'dan removes forces from the campaign for his own purpose, weakening the Horde.
phases.narration: The hidden bargain at the Horde's birth had never produced one purpose. Gul'dan turned away at the hour of greatest need, and the strength taken from the main host opened a fracture no command could simply close.

phases.title: A commander falls and an army rises
phases.summary: Lothar dies near Blackrock Spire; Turalyon rallies the Alliance rather than allowing it to break.
phases.narration: Near Blackrock, the Alliance lost the man who had carried Stormwind's warning north. Grief might have ended the advance. Turalyon made it a summons, and the army moved again with its memory before it.

phases.title: The tide returns toward the gate
phases.summary: The Alliance drives the weakened Horde south from Blackrock toward the Dark Portal.
phases.narration: The road of invasion reversed. The coalition that had formed from one kingdom's ruin passed through Blackrock and pressed south, while the Horde's remaining order narrowed around retreat and survival.

phases.title: The gateway is broken
phases.summary: The Alliance defeats the Horde at the threshold and destroys the original Dark Portal.
phases.narration: At the threshold between worlds, victory closed the road but not its consequences. The portal fell, many orcs entered captivity, and two peoples inherited a rivalry whose causes reached back to choices made beneath another sky.

outcome.summary: The Alliance defeated the Old Horde, destroyed the original Dark Portal, and imprisoned many surviving orcs; the political and human consequences carried forward toward the Third War.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The Second War spanned land, sea, air, and many engagements. No single battlefield marker or complete exact route is asserted.

battles.name: The Titan-forged War against the Black Empire

date.label: After the titan-forged were mustered

battles.summary: Keeper-led armies of stone and metal fought across primordial Azeroth, defeated the Black Empire's forces, and subdued the powers that had ruled the world.
battles.description: This title groups a world-spanning campaign described across Chronicle's Ordering sequence. The sources do not establish a surveyable front or one battle coordinate, so the atlas provides phases without an invented route or marker.

objectives.summary: Break the Black Empire while preserving Azeroth's nascent world-soul.
Hold the Old Gods' dominion against the keeper-led invasion.

phases.title: The keepers lead the hosts
phases.summary: Empowered keepers direct the first titan-forged armies into the corrupted world.
phases.narration: The keepers went before the hosts of living stone and metal. They did not come to conquer a kingdom for themselves, but to reach the power buried beneath it without destroying the world they had been made to save.

phases.title: The elemental powers are subdued
phases.summary: The titan-forged overcome the elemental forces bound to the Old Gods.
phases.narration: Storm, flame, stone, and sea rose against the invaders under the Old Gods' dominion. One by one those ancient powers were overcome, and the keepers prepared realms apart from the waking world in which the elemental hosts could be confined.

phases.title: The citadels are broken
phases.summary: The keeper-led hosts dismantle the Black Empire's military dominion.
phases.narration: Across unnamed fronts, the Black Empire's fortresses and servant hosts yielded. The sources give no single road by which the victory came, only a widening collapse as the titan-forged pressed toward the Old Gods themselves.

phases.title: The surviving Old Gods are bound
phases.summary: The remaining Old Gods are defeated and contained rather than torn from the world.
phases.narration: The lesson of the world-wound could not be ignored. The surviving Old Gods were not pulled free. They were overcome, chained, and sealed beneath Azeroth, so that their roots might remain without tearing the sleeping titan apart.

phases.title: A wounded world remains
phases.summary: Victory ends the empire but leaves a planet requiring containment and repair.
phases.narration: The empire had fallen, yet victory was not wholeness. Prisons lay beneath the earth, a wound burned at the continent's heart, and the keepers turned from war toward the longer labor of making Azeroth stable again.

outcome.summary: The Black Empire's rule was broken; its elemental powers were confined, the surviving Old Gods were imprisoned, and the keepers could begin healing and ordering Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Chronicle describes a world-spanning campaign but does not provide an exact battle site, front line, or campaign route. No marker is asserted.

battles.name: The Troll–Aqir War

date.label: After the aqir awakening

battles.summary: A long, multi-front struggle in which the Empire of Zul resisted the aqir and pursued their retreating forces toward the distant reaches of Kalimdor.
battles.description: This dossier presents strategic phases rather than a tactical simulation. The surviving account supports broad directions and consequences, not a single battlefield path or exact front line.

objectives.summary: Unite the threatened troll peoples, survive the first assault, and drive the aqir away from their centers.
Break the emerging troll powers and spread through their territories.

phases.title: The buried danger returns
phases.summary: Aqir forces emerge and press into the divided lands of the troll peoples.
phases.narration: The first change was not a border but a pressure felt across many lands: an ancient enemy rising beneath a world that had begun to forget it.

phases.title: The trolls unite
phases.summary: Zandalari leadership draws several troll peoples into the Empire of Zul.
phases.narration: Old rivalries did not vanish, yet the threat made alliance possible. The coalition carried many peoples without making them one people.

phases.title: The pursuit crosses Kalimdor
phases.summary: Troll forces pursue the retreating aqir toward northern and southern refuges over generations of war.
phases.narration: The struggle widened beyond any single field. Its roads are represented only in broad direction, for no surviving account measures every march.

phases.title: One enemy becomes several powers
phases.summary: The aqir threat is broken apart, leaving separated successor populations entrenched at opposite reaches of the continent.
phases.narration: Victory did not empty the earth. It divided an enemy, leaving distant powers whose descendants would trouble later ages.

outcome.summary: The Empire of Zul survived and the aqir were driven into separated refuges; the troll coalition then loosened as its members occupied distant regions.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The conflict was world-spanning and its exact fronts are not reconstructed as a battlefield marker or route.

battles.name: The Troll Wars

date.label: Approximately 2,800 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

battles.summary: A multi-stage war in which the Amani offensive against Quel'Thalas drew the high elves and Arathor into a decisive alliance.
battles.description: This dossier presents the political and strategic sequence rather than exact troop movements. The sources support an assault, alliance, transfer of arcane knowledge, and allied victory, but not a surveyed front line suitable for a single battle marker.

objectives.summary: Break the high-elven occupation and recover control over contested ancestral lands.
Preserve the kingdom and Sunwell against an overwhelming offensive.
Honor the wartime compact and prevent Amani power from threatening the united human nation.

phases.title: The northern war widens
phases.summary: Amani pressure grows into an assault that Quel'Thalas cannot safely contain alone.
phases.narration: The forest war was not born upon an empty map. Two peoples claimed memory in the same northern lands, and the old contest returned with strength enough to threaten the kingdom around the Sunwell.

phases.title: Need makes an alliance
phases.summary: Quel'Thalas seeks Arathor's aid and offers limited arcane instruction in return.
phases.narration: Distance and distrust yielded to necessity. The high elves opened a guarded portion of their learning; Arathor committed the weight of a nation that had only recently learned to stand as one.

phases.title: A new art enters human history
phases.summary: A limited company of humans trained in arcane magic joins the allied campaign.
phases.narration: The exchange outlived the emergency that created it. Fire answered the forest host, and human history acquired a power whose consequences would reach far beyond this war.

phases.title: Two powers converge
phases.summary: High-elven and Arathorian forces combine their strengths against the Amani campaign.
phases.narration: Neither ally fought as an ornament to the other. One brought knowledge of the northern land and arcane war; the other brought numbers, cohesion, and Thoradin's command.

phases.title: Victory changes the north
phases.summary: The allies win decisively and Amani regional power is reduced, though the Amani endure.
phases.narration: The offensive ended in defeat, but not in the disappearance of a people. The Amani endured with memory sharpened by loss, while their victors entered a season of expansion.

outcome.summary: Quel'Thalas and Arathor defeated the immediate Amani campaign; Amani power was greatly reduced, the high-elven kingdom survived, and arcane practice took root among humans.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The war contained several movements and engagements. No single exact battlefield point or tactical route is asserted.

battles.name: The Visions of N'Zoth Campaign

date.label: After N'Zoth's release

battles.summary: A strategic dossier of N'Zoth's assaults, the defense of mind and world, and the campaign into Ny'alotha.

phases.title: The prison opens
phases.summary: N'Zoth's release turns hidden pressure into open assault.
phases.narration: What had whispered beneath history stepped into its open page, and the wounded world found no shelter in disbelief.

phases.title: Assaults fall upon the world
phases.summary: Forces of the Old God attack key regions while corruption spreads through vision and fear.
phases.narration: The assault was made against walls and wills together; the map's violet shadows mark pressure, not measured borders.

phases.title: The defenders learn to endure the visions
phases.summary: Champions prepare to resist corruption while answering the assaults.
phases.narration: To reach the enemy, the defenders first had to carry an answer within themselves.

phases.title: The campaign enters Ny'alotha
phases.summary: The struggle crosses into N'Zoth's terrible domain.
phases.narration: The atlas cannot place that nightmare as an ordinary province. It names the crossing and refuses a false geography.

phases.title: The immediate assault is ended
phases.summary: N'Zoth is defeated and the campaign closes.
phases.narration: The vision broke and the world remained—scarred, uncertain, and soon to face a wound in the boundary of death itself.

outcome.summary: Champions defeated N'Zoth and ended his immediate assault on Azeroth.

battles.geographicEditorNote: Ny'alotha is not treated as a conventional measured place, and the multi-region campaign has no single exact marker.

battles.name: The War Against the Burning Legion

date.label: From the Broken Isles campaign through Argus

battles.summary: A cross-world strategic dossier from the Legion's return to the coalition's campaign on Argus.
battles.description: This dossier changes worldspaces rather than drawing a false geographic route between Azeroth and Argus.

phases.title: The Legion returns through the Broken Isles
phases.summary: A renewed invasion establishes the Broken Isles as its opening theater.
phases.narration: The old enemy returned not as a rumor of ancient ruin, but as armies beneath a green and wounded sky.

phases.title: The orders answer separately and together
phases.summary: Distinct orders gather champions when familiar institutions cannot carry the whole defense.
phases.narration: Different callings kept their own halls and names, yet turned their strength toward one survival.

phases.title: The Broken Isles campaign opens the way
phases.summary: The defense develops the means to carry the war beyond Azeroth.
phases.narration: Island by island, the defense became an answer bold enough to cross the boundary between worlds.

phases.title: The atlas turns to shattered Argus
phases.summary: The coalition reaches the Legion's ancient seat without a false line between worlds.
phases.narration: No ocean joined these shores. The atlas closes one measure and opens another upon a world long held in ruin.

phases.title: The crusade is broken at its source
phases.summary: The Argus campaign ends the Legion's immediate cosmic crusade.
phases.narration: Upon the broken world, old exiles and new champions carried the war to its source, and an age-long crusade lost the certainty of return.

outcome.summary: The coalition's campaign on Argus broke the Burning Legion's immediate crusade.

battles.geographicEditorNote: This cross-world campaign is deliberately not assigned one geographic marker.

battles.name: The War of the Ancients

date.label: c. 10,000 years before the Dark Portal

battles.summary: A continent-spanning war in which the Burning Legion devastated ancient Kalimdor before a changing alliance disrupted the gateway at the Well.
battles.description: This dossier presents five strategic phases rather than a tactical simulation. The invasion crossed many places and involved many participants; the surviving account does not support one exact battlefield marker or a single continuous front line.

objectives.summary: Secure the gateway, destroy resistance across Kalimdor, and enable Sargeras to enter Azeroth.
Sustain and enlarge the portal at the Well in service of Azshara's alliance with the Legion.
Survive the invasion, gather allies, and disrupt the gateway before Sargeras can cross.

phases.title: The court opens the gate
phases.summary: The Highborne channel the Well into a portal and Legion forces enter through Zin-Azshari.
phases.narration: The empire's center became the road of its undoing. From the Well, the invasion widened across lands still joined beneath one sky.

phases.title: A divided people resists
phases.summary: Kaldorei opponents of Azshara organize and converge while the invasion spreads.
phases.narration: There was no single untouched road to victory. Defenders gathered through burning country, carrying different loyalties toward one necessity.

phases.title: The living world enters the war
phases.summary: Cenarius and other ancient powers join the defense while the Dragon Aspects prepare the Dragon Soul.
phases.narration: Forest, wing, and mortal courage stood together, for the Legion's victory would leave no separate realm in which any could endure.

phases.title: The weapon turns upon its makers
phases.summary: Neltharion uses the Dragon Soul against allies as well as enemies, breaking the dragons' unity.
phases.narration: A weapon made by many answered to one corrupted will. In the hour of alliance, betrayal opened another wound within the defense.

phases.title: All roads return to the Well
phases.summary: The defenders converge on the gateway and disrupt it before Sargeras can enter Azeroth.
phases.narration: At last the war returned to the water from which the empire's power had risen. The gate was broken, but the world beneath it could not remain whole.

outcome.summary: The Legion's immediate invasion was stopped and Sargeras did not enter Azeroth, but the Well collapsed and the resulting Sundering destroyed the old continental world.

battles.geographicEditorNote: The war was continent-spanning. Only the Well and Zin-Azshari receive approximate location context; the battle itself has no exact marker.

battles.name: The War of the Three Hammers

date.label: Approximately 230 years before the Dark Portal; working chronology

battles.summary: A dwarven succession war drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from Ironforge, opened new centers, and ended when Ragnaros's return devastated the southern mountains.
battles.description: The dossier joins two connected phases of civil conflict at strategic scale. It does not treat Ironforge, Grim Batol, the Redridge front, and the volcanic aftermath as one exact battlefield.

objectives.summary: Competing clans sought control, survival, or revenge across Ironforge and the strongholds founded after the first expulsion.

phases.title: One mountain loses its center
phases.summary: The high king's death breaks the balance among the three clans.
phases.narration: A mountain that had contained many loyalties could not contain their claims once its old center failed. Kinship became a line of battle beneath the stone.

phases.title: Ironforge chooses a victor
phases.summary: The Bronzebeards retain the city while the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans are expelled.
phases.narration: Victory kept one clan beneath the mountain and sent two others into landscapes where grievance would harden into new identities.

phases.title: Defeat becomes new kingdoms
phases.summary: The Wildhammers establish Grim Batol while the Dark Irons establish Thaurissan farther south.
phases.narration: Exile did not end either people. New halls rose north and south, and the old quarrel acquired distance without acquiring peace.

phases.title: Revenge opens two fronts
phases.summary: Dark Iron armies strike toward both Ironforge and Grim Batol and are driven back.
phases.narration: The war returned along two roads. Former rivals answered the same danger, and the armies of the deep were broken between the powers they had meant to defeat apart.

phases.title: The earth answers the last summons
phases.summary: A desperate summoning brings Ragnaros into the world and transforms the southern mountains.
phases.narration: At the edge of defeat, a call went downward into powers older than every dwarven throne. The answer ended the war by making the land itself more terrible than victory.

outcome.summary: The Bronzebeards retained Ironforge, the Wildhammers and Dark Irons formed separate centers, and Ragnaros's return devastated the southern mountains and subjected surviving Dark Irons to a new power.

battles.geographicEditorNote: This was a dispersed civil war across multiple strongholds and later fronts; the atlas therefore uses only an inferred dispersal route and approximate place markers.

storyGuides.title: The Roads Open Before the Unnumbered
storyGuides.description: A continuous history from Ahn'Qiraj through Outland, Northrend, the Cataclysm, Pandaria, alternate Draenor, and the final campaign against the Burning Legion.

storyGuides.title: Crowns Before the Sundering
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the first troll powers, the war with the aqir, the southern empire and its fall, and the kaldorei ascent that placed ancient Kalimdor on the threshold of catastrophe.

storyGuides.title: The Rise of the Black Empire
storyGuides.description: A guided history of primordial Azeroth, its elemental wars, the Old Gods' arrival, and the rise of the Black Empire.

storyGuides.title: Before the First World Was Ordered
storyGuides.description: A continuous guided history from Chronicle's primordial cosmic powers through the birth of the universe, the awakening of the titans, and the design that sent the Old Gods toward worlds such as Azeroth.

storyGuides.title: The Shores That Learned New Names
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the Long Vigil, the Highborne exile, Quel'Thalas, Arathor and the Troll Wars, the Seven Kingdoms, and the dwarven war that remade the southern mountains.

storyGuides.title: Where the World's Wounds Open Outward
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the Fourth War, N'Zoth, the Shadowlands, the Dragon Isles, Khaz Algar, and the announced horizon of Midnight.

storyGuides.title: The Wounding and Ordering of Azeroth
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the Pantheon's discovery, the costly first intervention, the titan-forged war, the containment of the Old Gods, and the long work that transformed a conquered world into ancient Kalimdor.

storyGuides.title: The Road That Crossed the Stars
storyGuides.description: A continuous cross-world history of Draenor's manipulation, the Old Horde, the Dark Portal, Stormwind's fall, the Alliance of Lordaeron, and the Second War's reversal.

storyGuides.title: When the Northern Lamps Went Dark
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of the Scourge crisis, Arthas's fall, the Legion's return, the defense of Mount Hyjal, and the road through Outland to the Frozen Throne.

storyGuides.title: When the World Was Broken
storyGuides.description: A continuous history of Azshara's court, the Legion invasion, the defenders of ancient Kalimdor, the betrayal of Neltharion, and the Sundering that remade the world.

storyNodes.title: The great powers call upon unnumbered hands
storyNodes.narration: The age opened without a single crowned hero at its center. At Ahn'Qiraj, Alliance and Horde communities gathered a vast war effort while independent champions prepared to cross the opened gates. Their fellowship was temporary, their motives varied, and the atlas names them only as adventurers: an interpretive company standing for the many who entered dangers that armies alone had not resolved.

storyNodes.title: The road crosses into a broken world
storyNodes.narration: The Dark Portal opened again, and the chronicle changed its ground. Outland was not a distant province on Azeroth's sea, but the remains of Draenor under another sky. The atlas therefore closes one worldspace and opens another. Across that shattered land, old exiles, demonic powers, and new expeditions met within consequences already centuries in the making.

storyNodes.title: The northern crown receives its reckoning
storyNodes.narration: The next great campaign returned to Azeroth and climbed through Northrend toward Icecrown. Arthas had once crossed this cold seeking the strength to save his kingdom; now others followed the ruin of that choice to its throne. The stages shown are strategic memory, not a raid plan. At the citadel's height, the Lich King's reign ended, though the burdens bound to Northrend did not vanish with him.

storyNodes.title: The earth remembers its betrayed guardian
storyNodes.narration: Then Deathwing returned, and the land itself became testimony. Coasts broke, mountains opened, and old regions entered a new state that could not honestly be shown as a mere overlay upon yesterday. The scarred terrain before you is interpretive rather than surveyed. Its purpose is to make one consequence unmistakable: Azeroth after the Cataclysm was not the same world the northern victors had left behind.

storyNodes.title: A hidden land receives an old quarrel
storyNodes.narration: Beyond the Cataclysm's upheaval, Pandaria returned to the wider world's knowledge. Its peoples and landscapes were not an empty stage awaiting foreign banners. Yet Alliance and Horde carried their rivalry ashore, and the consequences deepened within a land that had long endured histories of its own. The atlas holds Pandaria as a place encountered, not discovered into existence by those who arrived from elsewhere.

storyNodes.title: The war turns upon its own warchief
storyNodes.narration: The conflict carried home from Pandaria did not leave the Horde whole. Opposition to Garrosh's rule gathered within it while Alliance forces advanced upon Orgrimmar. Their purposes met in a siege that ended his leadership, not in a simple reconciliation of every grievance. The city marker is only a narrative anchor; the greater change was political, dividing obedience from belonging and leaving another unsettled road ahead.

storyNodes.title: History opens beside itself
storyNodes.narration: The next invasion came from an alternate Draenor: neither the intact world remembered in earlier centuries nor the Outland made by its destruction. Iron and ambition had formed the Iron Horde there. A separate worldspace keeps that distinction visible. This terrain is an interpretive echo of unbroken Draenor, while the anonymous war host represents an embodied power rather than any one named commander or exact camp.

storyNodes.title: The ancient enemy returns to the Broken Isles
storyNodes.narration: From the alternate war's ending rose the way for an older enemy to return. The Burning Legion invaded through the Broken Isles. Established armies could not answer every wound, and distinct class orders gathered champions according to calling rather than kingdom. The ensemble before you is symbolic: many orders, many traditions, one immediate necessity. Beside them stood Illidan, carrying his own long and perilous history into the defense.

storyNodes.title: The defenders carry the war to Argus
storyNodes.narration: Defense became pursuit, and pursuit crossed the dark between worlds. Argus appears in its own atlas measure: a shattered realm of broken plateaus and fel-lit wounds, rendered as interpretive terrain rather than surveyed fact. There old exiles, the Army of the Light, Illidan, and Azeroth's champions struck at the Legion's seat. No geographic line joins the worlds; the change of state tells the crossing honestly.

storyNodes.title: Victory returns to a wounded world
storyNodes.narration: The Legion's immediate crusade was broken on Argus, and the age of far roads reached its sternest victory. Yet those roads led home to no untouched morning. Azeroth had endured the Scourge, the Cataclysm, faction war, and powers from beyond its sky. The champions who had crossed so many thresholds returned to a world whose wounds would become causes in their own right—and whose next war would begin before healing was complete.

storyNodes.title: The ordered world begins to remember
storyNodes.narration: When the distant makers had gone, the world did not fall silent. Rivers carried soil from the new mountains, forests gathered beneath the rain, and living things multiplied around the power of the Well. The keepers had shaped a place where history could begin. Now its peoples would give the land memory, rivalry, law, and names of their own.

storyNodes.title: Many peoples beneath one sky
storyNodes.narration: Across forest, jungle, and high country, troll peoples flourished. The Zandalar raised their center among the mountains, while other great tribes gathered strength in lands of their own. They shared old devotions, yet no single throne bound them. Their rivalries were real, but so was the knowledge that each belonged to a world older and wider than any one hunting ground.

storyNodes.title: The earth gives back an ancient enemy
storyNodes.narration: Then the old darkness moved again. The aqir, heirs of a buried and terrible age, surged against the growing troll lands. This danger was not another quarrel over a valley or river. It threatened every separate power at once, and taught the scattered tribes that survival might demand a name greater than any of their own.

storyNodes.title: The Empire of Zul stands together
storyNodes.narration: Under Zandalari leadership, the tribes entered a wartime union remembered as the Empire of Zul. It was alliance, not sameness: forest, jungle, ice, and highland peoples carried their own customs into the struggle. Together they survived the first pressure, then followed the retreating aqir across distances too great for any honest map to draw as a single road.

storyNodes.title: Victory scatters both enemy and ally
storyNodes.narration: At last the aqir withdrew into far northern and southern refuges. There, separation remade them into powers with futures of their own. The troll armies likewise remained in the lands they had won. With the common danger broken, the old coalition loosened, and distance began to turn fellow victors into distinct empires with separate memories.

storyNodes.title: The south becomes a world of kings
storyNodes.narration: In the south, another inheritance was unraveling. The keepers' servants had once worked toward appointed purposes, but silence and long ages divided the mogu into rival kingdoms. They contended across the lands that would one day be called Pandaria, each ruler seeking mastery while the older order receded into half-remembered command.

storyNodes.title: One king takes the storm
storyNodes.narration: From that age of divided kings rose Lei Shen. Through power, calculation, and conquest, he broke his rivals and made the mogu kneel to one emperor. The unity he forged was not the keepers' stewardship restored. It was a new dominion, centered on his will and armed with powers taken from an older world.

storyNodes.title: An empire is built upon obedience
storyNodes.narration: The mogu empire spread across the southern lands. Peoples who had kept languages, crafts, and histories of their own were made to serve its monuments and wars. Among them were the pandaren. The empire's roads and walls declared permanence, yet every generation forced into silence carried another memory of life before the throne.

storyNodes.title: Empty hands become a promise
storyNodes.narration: Kang looked upon a people denied weapons and found strength the empire had overlooked. An unarmed discipline could be practiced, taught, and carried where blades could not. Resistance spread from lesson to fellowship, and from one subjected people to many. The mogu order, made vast by obedience, broke when those beneath it learned to stand together.

storyNodes.title: A people apart follows the water
storyNodes.narration: Far from empire and coalition, a nocturnal troll people kept to hidden places and their own company. In time they came toward the heart of Kalimdor, where the Well shone like a fallen heaven upon the earth. They did not know that dwelling beside its waters would change more than their home. It would change the shape of history itself.

storyNodes.title: Around the Well, the kaldorei arise
storyNodes.narration: Generations passed beneath the Well's radiance. The people changed, and called themselves kaldorei. Curiosity became study; study became sorcery, cities, and roads. Their power carried them outward with astonishing speed. Older troll dominions yielded before them, until a civilization born beside one lake stood over much of the continent that had once seemed beyond measure.

storyNodes.title: A queen at the edge of ruin
storyNodes.narration: At the height of this rising world, Azshara took the throne. Admiration gathered around her like light upon still water, and the most gifted of the kaldorei drew close to her court and to the Well. Ancient Kalimdor appeared united beneath splendor. Yet power had narrowed toward one queen, one circle, and one inexhaustible source. Beyond that bright horizon waited war and sundering.

storyNodes.title: Before the empire
storyNodes.narration: Before mountain or sea had received a name, Azeroth's tale had already begun amid powers vaster than the world. Chronicle sets Light against Shadow, Life against Death, and Order against Disorder, while fire, air, earth, water, Spirit, and Decay shaped the mortal realm.

storyNodes.title: The sleeping titan within
storyNodes.narration: Deep within the young world, unseen beneath stone and flame, a mighty titan spirit stirred. As it grew, it drew heavily upon Spirit, the fifth element; and without that gentle balance, the native powers of Azeroth became restless and untamed.

storyNodes.title: Four powers without balance
storyNodes.narration: Four great lords arose above the tumult: Al'Akir, master of air; Ragnaros, lord of fire; Therazane, mother of earth; and Neptulon, ruler of water. Each desired dominion, and each carried war according to the nature of their element.

storyNodes.title: An age of elemental war
storyNodes.narration: Age followed uncounted age beneath storm, flood, fire, and heaving stone. The elemental hosts broke one another's realms and raised them anew, yet no victory endured; strife itself became the rhythm of primordial Azeroth.

storyNodes.title: The Old Gods descend
storyNodes.narration: Then the long contest was broken by a terror from beyond the heavens. The Old Gods fell from the Great Dark and rooted themselves in Azeroth. Around them the land withered, while their deep-reaching tendrils sought the sleeping world-soul below.

storyNodes.title: The empire's builders
storyNodes.narration: From the corrupted substance of the Old Gods arose servants shaped for their dark labor. The cunning n'raqi became taskmasters, and beneath their command the enduring aqir raised vast citadels and temple cities around their terrible masters.

storyNodes.title: A bastion near the world's center
storyNodes.narration: Greatest among those strongholds stood the bastion raised about Y'Shaarj, near the heart of Azeroth's largest continent. Its light upon this map is only approximate: Chronicle names its place in relation to the continent, but grants neither exact measure nor a proper city name.

storyNodes.title: The Black Empire spreads
storyNodes.narration: From that dreadful heart, the holdings of Y'Shaarj and the domains of the other Old Gods spread until together they formed the Black Empire. The boundary now revealed is a broad reconstruction of influence, not a surveyed frontier preserved by the source.

storyNodes.title: Old rivals form one resistance
storyNodes.narration: At last the ancient rivals beheld an enemy that threatened them all. For the first time the Elemental Lords stood together: wind bore fire against the empire, and earth rose against its cities. Yet even their joined wrath could not win the age.

storyNodes.title: A world awaiting the Ordering
storyNodes.narration: The Elemental Lords were defeated and bound, and the shadow of the Black Empire crept across much of Azeroth. Thus the primordial age darkened toward its end, until the Pantheon perceived the peril and sent titan-forged armies to answer it.

storyNodes.title: Before time could be counted
storyNodes.narration: Before any world carried mountain, sea, or name, Chronicle begins with a boundless opposition. Light shone without measure, and beyond its reach gathered Shadow—the Void. They were not kingdoms upon a chart, but primordial powers, divided in nature and bound within the first telling of the cosmos.

storyNodes.title: The Great Dark opens
storyNodes.narration: Where Light and Void pressed against one another, their conflict broke the stillness. From that violence came the physical universe: the Great Dark Beyond, immense and cold, kindled with newborn stars. Here at last were distance and matter, though no mortal witness stood beneath those first and ancient fires.

storyNodes.title: A storm beside creation
storyNodes.narration: Yet creation did not settle into silence. Unstable energies gathered into the Twisting Nether, a volatile astral realm interwoven with the Great Dark and unlike its ordered substance. The nearness shown here is only the nearness of one thought to the next; no source grants these realms a measured border.

storyNodes.title: Powers that shape reality
storyNodes.narration: Across this vast account stand six great forces. Light answers Shadow; Life answers Death; Order answers Disorder. Fire, air, earth, water, Spirit, and Decay move within the mortal realm beneath them. This is Chronicle's framework, offered here as a lantern for the story—not as the last word on every mystery.

storyNodes.title: Dreamers in the deep
storyNodes.narration: Among the countless worlds, some bore a presence hidden far below their crust: a titan spirit, sleeping while ages passed above. Such world-souls grew slowly within their wandering homes. If one endured and awakened, it rose no longer as a world alone, but as a living titan of immeasurable power.

storyNodes.title: The first titan wakes
storyNodes.narration: First among them to wake was Aman’Thul. He looked into the lonely reaches of the Great Dark and understood that others of his kind might still dream within distant worlds. So the Highfather began his long search, crossing the newborn heavens and calling to the spirits he found sleeping there.

storyNodes.title: The Pantheon gathers
storyNodes.narration: One by one, awakened titans answered, until Aman’Thul no longer walked the cosmos alone. Together they became the Pantheon. Where they found worlds wounded or disordered, they labored to bring stability; and beyond each ordered horizon, they continued the search for brethren who had not yet opened their eyes.

storyNodes.title: A design cast into darkness
storyNodes.narration: The Void Lords also sought the sleeping titans, but could not pour their full strength into the physical universe. In their hunger they shaped the Old Gods and hurled them blindly through the Great Dark. Their hope was dreadful and patient: that one might strike a world-soul and corrupt it before awakening.

storyNodes.title: One world among the stars
storyNodes.narration: Across that immeasurable dark turned a young world called Azeroth, bearing within it a titan spirit of extraordinary might. The Old Gods would find this world before the Pantheon understood its peril. There the cosmic design narrowed into earth, flame, storm, and sea—and the long age of the Black Empire drew near.

storyNodes.title: The broken world waits for new promises
storyNodes.narration: The survivors at Hyjal looked upon a world whose distances had become seas. At the center, the Maelstrom kept the wound of the Sundering open to every horizon. Around the mountain there was safety enough to endure, but no return to the old empire. Whatever order followed would have to be made among separated shores, scattered peoples, and memories too heavy to become a single law.

storyNodes.title: One vial restores the danger beneath Hyjal
storyNodes.narration: Illidan had carried water away from the first Well before it died. Upon Hyjal he poured that preserved power into a mountain lake, and another Well came into being beneath a world still grieving the first. To him it was a weapon against the Legion's return. To those who discovered it, the act reopened the very danger for which a continent had paid. Judgment followed, and Illidan was taken from the daylight of the new age.

storyNodes.title: A tree is set above the forbidden water
storyNodes.narration: The answer was not to spill another sea across the earth. Nordrassil was planted over the new Well, and the great powers of the dragons bound gifts and safeguards to the living tree. Malfurion and Tyrande stood at the beginning of a people remade by duty: one path turning toward the deep dream of the world, another remaining wakeful beneath moon and leaf. The refuge became a charge that would endure beyond kingdoms.

storyNodes.title: The long watch gathers beneath the boughs
storyNodes.narration: Thus began the Long Vigil. The kaldorei guarded Kalimdor and prepared for an enemy that might not return within any mortal lifetime. Yet the watch was not one unchanging army. Priests, sentinels, druids, wardens, and many quiet keepers bore different parts of the burden while forests grew over the scars of war. Their strength was patience; their danger was believing that one people's answer must bind every survivor.

storyNodes.title: A forbidden art divides the survivors
storyNodes.narration: Not every Highborne accepted the ban upon arcane practice. To them, magic was not only the queen's ruin; it was knowledge, inheritance, and the means by which their people had once shaped the world. Conflict answered prohibition, and exile answered conflict. Under Dath'Remar, they departed the forests of Kalimdor. The decision protected one new order by sending another people away to seek a shore where their art might live.

storyNodes.title: The exiles cross a sea made by yesterday
storyNodes.narration: Their road crossed the waters that the Sundering had made. No surviving atlas measures every storm, landing, or generation of that passage, and the line shown here is only a direction between loss and settlement. Dath'Remar's company carried families as well as scholars, memory as well as ambition. By the time they reached the northern east, exile had begun to transform a courtly caste into a people seeking a homeland.

storyNodes.title: A new sun rises upon contested land
storyNodes.narration: In the northern Eastern Kingdoms the exiles founded Quel'Thalas and kindled the Sunwell from power carried out of the old world. But the land was not empty, and founding was not the first history written there. The Amani held ancestral claims to the same northern forests. The bright new kingdom and the enduring troll power therefore grew beside one another in a peace burdened from its beginning by incompatible memories of home.

storyNodes.title: Scattered tribes answer one human king
storyNodes.narration: Farther south, human communities had multiplied without yet becoming one nation. Thoradin gathered them beneath a common banner and raised Arathor around the fortress of Strom. The new unity did not erase every tribe or custom; it made their strength answer together when danger crossed old boundaries. Humanity had gained a political center at the same hour that the northern conflict was growing too great for Quel'Thalas to bear alone.

storyNodes.title: Need joins two young powers
storyNodes.narration: When the Amani offensive threatened to overwhelm Quel'Thalas, the high elves turned to Arathor. Neither people offered aid without consequence. A chosen company of humans received arcane teaching, and Thoradin committed his nation's strength to the northern war. The compact joined realms separated by custom and lifespan because each could provide what the other lacked. It also placed magic within human history, where it would never again remain a foreign wonder.

storyNodes.title: Fire changes the forest and human history
storyNodes.narration: The allied campaign ended the immediate Amani assault and broke much of the empire's regional power. Yet defeat did not erase the Amani, their memory, or their claim to the north. Quel'Thalas survived, and Arathor emerged with its unity proven in war. More quietly, the arcane art taught for one emergency took root among humans. A military victory had altered three futures: the victors', the defeated people's, and magic's place in the mortal world.

storyNodes.title: One human empire becomes seven kingdoms
storyNodes.narration: Arathor's victory did not preserve its center forever. Roads lengthened, ports prospered, city-states acquired customs and interests of their own, and Strom's authority weakened across generations. No single morning raised seven crowns at once. The change was slower: one common realm becoming several sovereign powers until the old unity survived chiefly as ancestry and memory. The late map therefore shows a broad plurality, not borders frozen upon one date.

storyNodes.title: Three hammers break one mountain realm
storyNodes.narration: Within Ironforge, the death of an old high king released rival claims among Bronzebeard, Wildhammer, and Dark Iron. War left the Bronzebeards beneath the mountain and sent the others toward new strongholds: Grim Batol in the north and Thaurissan in the south. The route shown is not one march. It is the shape of a people dividing, carrying kinship and grievance into separate halls where neither distance nor time was enough to settle the first defeat.

storyNodes.title: An ancient fire answers a dying war
storyNodes.narration: The Dark Irons returned against both rival realms, and their armies were driven toward ruin. In desperation, a summons reached powers sleeping far below every dwarven quarrel. Ragnaros answered. The Firelord's return shattered the southern mountains, destroyed the hand that had called him, and placed the surviving Dark Irons beneath a more terrible dominion. The civil war ended not by restoring unity, but by awakening the primordial world inside the new one.

storyNodes.title: Many realms stand before an unopened gate
storyNodes.narration: At the close of this long age, no single power held the world that the Sundering had divided. The kaldorei kept their vigil in Kalimdor. Quel'Thalas guarded its northern light beside an undefeated memory of Amani loss. Human kingdoms inherited Arathor without its unity, and the dwarven clans carried one ancestry into separate halls. Beyond their knowledge, another history was gathering on Draenor. Soon a gate would join the worlds, and every settled border would be tested.

storyNodes.title: The wounded inherit another war
storyNodes.narration: Victory over the Legion did not quiet the world. Alliance and Horde entered a new war across distant footholds, carrying grief, fear, and old distrust into regions that possessed their own histories. The two broad fields on this atlas do not claim territorial borders. They mark a conflict too wide for one battlefield and too entangled to be explained as the will of one people alone.

storyNodes.title: A people turns against its warchief
storyNodes.narration: Within the Horde, loyalty to community and obedience to Sylvanas no longer led along the same road. Rebellion gathered, and Alliance pressure converged with it against her rule. The war campaign ended, but its dead did not return and its broken trust did not mend at a command. History moved on because actors chose an ending; consequence remained because no choice could restore what the war had taken.

storyNodes.title: The last prison opens beneath the wounds
storyNodes.narration: N'Zoth emerged into a world already strained by war. Assaults struck more than fortifications; they pressed upon perception, memory, and will. The violet region spread across this map is not a border of empire. It is an interpretive field of pressure, for Ny'alotha cannot honestly be placed as an ordinary neighboring province. The oldest darkness returned by making uncertainty itself part of the battlefield.

storyNodes.title: The nightmare is entered and broken
storyNodes.narration: To end the assault, champions carried the struggle into Ny'alotha. This chronicle records the crossing and the outcome without pretending the nightmare has ordinary coordinates or reducing it to encounter steps. N'Zoth's immediate campaign was defeated. Yet the relief was brief: the world had scarcely turned from an Old God's visions when another boundary—the veil between life and death—was violently opened.

storyNodes.title: The sky above Icecrown is torn
storyNodes.narration: Sylvanas shattered the veil, and the next road did not cross an ocean or portal into another material world. It descended into the realms of death. The field before you is deliberately relational: distinct domains gather around a central waystation through luminous bonds. Distance, direction, and adjacency are symbolic. Here the atlas abandons terrain rather than disguise metaphysical relationship as conventional geography.

storyNodes.title: Four realms keep their separate callings
storyNodes.narration: Within the Shadowlands, the covenants were not interchangeable colors upon one realm. Each carried its own duty, memory, and crisis. The four envoys shown here are anonymous symbols, composed to keep those differences embodied without claiming a canonical meeting. Mortal champions moved among their campaigns, and distinct powers found reasons to resist a danger that had reached through the order of death itself.

storyNodes.title: The ancient isles awaken to a changed world
storyNodes.narration: After the journey beyond death, the Dragon Isles awakened and called the dragonflights home. Their return was not merely a recovery of forgotten ground. It reopened questions of inheritance, purpose, and the meaning of guardianship in an age when Azeroth's oldest institutions had repeatedly failed or changed. The five dragons spiral symbolically above an approximate island focus; they are the flights remembered together, not one literal formation.

storyNodes.title: The warning descends beneath Khaz Algar
storyNodes.narration: The Worldsoul Saga opened in Khaz Algar, where surface and subterranean histories meet within one compressed atlas focus. Xal'atath gathered her designs while the Earthen revealed cultures shaped beyond the familiar kingdoms. The figure and ensemble are interpretive, but the uncertainty is not decorative: this chapter remains near the living edge of the archive, where evidence is newer and consequence has not yet settled into distant perspective.

storyNodes.title: The chronicle ends where announcement begins
storyNodes.narration: At this archive's present edge stands Midnight: announced, not concluded. Its premise turns Xal'atath's assault toward the blood elf homelands and names Eversong among the coming theaters. The shadow on the map is therefore a boundary of knowledge, not a predicted front. No victor is named, no fate presumed. The chronicle leaves the last road open, because honest history must know when tomorrow has not yet become its evidence.

storyNodes.title: The world the keepers inherited
storyNodes.narration: The tale begins where the Black Empire left the world: beneath a dominion of citadels, servant hosts, and powers rooted deeper than any mountain. Azeroth's sleeping spirit endured below them, mighty beyond measure and yet unable to cast the corruption from its own skin. Nothing upon the world remained strong enough to break that reign.

storyNodes.title: A watcher finds the hidden world
storyNodes.narration: Far beyond those clouded skies, Aggramar found Azeroth. He perceived the nascent titan within, and also the Old Gods fastening their will around it. The news passed to the Pantheon like a bell across the Great Dark. Here was a spirit of extraordinary promise; here too was a peril that could turn such promise against all creation.

storyNodes.title: Victory becomes a wound
storyNodes.narration: Aman’Thul reached toward the greatest of the Old Gods and tore Y'Shaarj from the world. The horror was destroyed, but its roots had entered too deeply. Stone, empire, and corruption came away together, and Azeroth's arcane lifeblood surged from the wound. In that instant the Pantheon learned that strength alone might kill the one it sought to save.

storyNodes.title: Hands of stone and metal
storyNodes.narration: The answer was not another titan's grasp. At Aggramar's urging, the Pantheon fashioned servants whose power could be brought against the Black Empire without shattering Azeroth beneath their feet. From stone and metal came the first titan-forged hosts: soldiers made for the war before them, and workers for labors not yet begun.

storyNodes.title: The keepers take command
storyNodes.narration: Among the titan-forged, the Pantheon raised a smaller company to bear greater power and judgment. These were the keepers. They would command the hosts, answer changing danger with more than brute force, and remain when distant makers had gone. Beneath their direction, the armies entered a world whose every horizon belonged to the enemy.

storyNodes.title: The long dominion breaks
storyNodes.narration: The war passed across fronts whose roads are no longer known. The titan-forged overcame the elemental powers bound to the Old Gods, broke servant hosts, and cast down the Black Empire's strongholds. No single stroke ended that shadow. It receded through a world-spanning campaign until the keepers stood before the powers beneath the empire itself.

storyNodes.title: Chains beneath the earth
storyNodes.narration: The surviving Old Gods could not be torn out without opening new wounds. Thus the keepers chose containment. The defeated horrors were bound in prisons beneath Azeroth, near enough to remain a danger, yet held from the sleeping titan's heart. Victory had not erased the corruption. It had made the long guarding of it possible.

storyNodes.title: The wound becomes a well
storyNodes.narration: At the continent's heart, Azeroth still bled light into the open world. The keepers labored around that ruin, raising wards until the torrent quieted and its power found balance. What remained was named the Well of Eternity: not a scar made beautiful, but a scar kept from becoming the death of the world.

storyNodes.title: Two forges hold the world
storyNodes.narration: The work spread from the Well toward two great engines. In the far north, Ulduar held the Forge of Wills. Far to the south stood the Forge of Origination, made both to strengthen the wounded world and, should corruption become absolute, to begin it anew. Between them passed the hidden labor of preservation.

storyNodes.title: Mountains rise, and rivers find the sea
storyNodes.narration: Then began the labor by which victory became a world. Titan-forged hands raised ranges, opened deep places, cut waterways, dredged seas, tended engines, and guarded what had been built. The keepers fostered places where living things could flourish. When they looked across the primary continent they had shaped, they called it Kalimdor, the land beneath eternal starlight.

storyNodes.title: The makers pass beyond the sky
storyNodes.narration: At last the Pantheon judged Azeroth guarded well enough to leave. The keepers remained beside their forges, prisons, and appointed works, while the titan-forged watched a quieter horizon. Yet the ordered world was no finished monument. Around the Well, life would change, gather memory, and raise powers of its own. The age of ancient civilizations waited beyond the dawn.

storyNodes.title: Draenor holds more than one remembered home
storyNodes.narration: Before there was a Horde, the orcs lived as many clans beneath Draenor's sky, bound by ancestry, rivalry, and the voices of the elements. The draenei also called this world home after a long exile among the stars. Their cities and the clans' hunting grounds did not make a perfect peace, yet neither people was born for the war that would consume them. The first map therefore shows coexistence before conspiracy.

storyNodes.title: An old vengeance finds a younger world
storyNodes.narration: Kil'jaeden had not forgotten the exiles who escaped him. When he found the draenei upon Draenor, he did not begin with an army descending openly from the heavens. He looked instead toward their neighbors. Orcish strength, clan loyalty, and reverence for ancestral counsel could all be turned if the warning appeared to come from a trusted voice. Thus a private hatred reached for an entire people as its instrument.

storyNodes.title: Trust becomes the first weapon
storyNodes.narration: Ner'zhul was heard because he had earned the clans' respect. Kil'jaeden preyed upon grief and presented deception in the likeness of ancestral counsel. Suspicion hardened into raids, and raids made the next accusation easier to believe. When Ner'zhul understood that the path before him did not lead where the ancestors had promised, he resisted—but by then fear already had its own momentum, and another apprentice was willing to continue.

storyNodes.title: A council grows behind the warchief's chair
storyNodes.narration: Gul'dan accepted what Ner'zhul would not. Around him gathered warlocks and agents whose authority was strongest when unseen. The Shadow Council helped turn many clans toward a single war while Blackhand stood before them as warchief. Unity came, but not as freely chosen kinship: command, fear, new magic, and concealed bargains bound the structure together. Draenor's political map had begun to narrow beneath a hand most warriors could not see.

storyNodes.title: Power is offered in a cup that remembers
storyNodes.narration: Before the last great assault, Mannoroth's blood was offered as strength. Many accepted, and the bargain deepened the Legion's hold upon the Horde. Yet the choice was not universal. Durotan refused it for the Frostwolves, preserving a witness that coercion had not erased every will. The distinction matters: the Horde was transformed by manipulation and decision, but no single cup can stand for every orc who lived beneath Draenor's darkening sky.

storyNodes.title: A bright city falls beneath a wounded sky
storyNodes.narration: The Horde's war broke upon Shattrath with terrible force. The city fell, organized resistance was shattered, and the draenei were reduced to scattered survivors—but they were not erased. Victory also failed to heal the conquerors' world. Fel practice and war had sickened the land, and the host built for one enemy now faced emptiness after conquest. A machine taught to hunger would soon be shown another world through another man's dream.

storyNodes.title: The road does not cross a map—it leaves a world
storyNodes.narration: Across the gulf between worlds, Medivh's corrupted will answered Gul'dan. Together their workings opened the Dark Portal. The atlas does not draw that passage as a road across oceans, for no shared geography joins these skies. It changes worldspace. Draenor falls away; Azeroth appears, and the same threshold stands in another land. Through it came scouts, warriors, and at last the weight of the Horde. The calendar of the modern wars begins here.

storyNodes.title: Stormwind discovers that the enemy has another sky
storyNodes.narration: The first war widened by returns. Early assaults could be resisted, but the Horde learned the southern kingdom while greater forces crossed behind them. Stormwind fought an enemy whose reserves lay beyond the edge of its world, even as Medivh's betrayal divided trust within its own defense. The line shown is only strategic direction from portal to kingdom. It does not turn many campaigns into one neat march, or game missions into surveyed history.

storyNodes.title: The hand behind the throne is struck
storyNodes.narration: The Horde's visible and hidden commands turned against one another during the war. Orgrim killed Blackhand, shattered much of the Shadow Council, and took the warchief's mantle himself. He opposed Gul'dan's private mastery, but he did not abandon the invasion. The war therefore changed leadership without changing its immediate direction. Stormwind still faced the army at its gates, now commanded by a leader who sought to make the Horde answer openly to him.

storyNodes.title: One kingdom falls, and its warning sails north
storyNodes.narration: Stormwind was taken and left in ruin. For the Horde, the First War ended in victory. For the survivors, defeat became a voyage: Lothar and those who escaped carried more than grief toward the northern kingdoms. They carried proof that isolation was no defense against a gate between worlds. The southern realm had fallen alone; whether its neighbors would remain separate became the next question upon which all their histories turned.

storyNodes.title: Seven inheritances become one wartime promise
storyNodes.narration: In Lordaeron, the warning met old rivalries, different interests, and the understandable hope that the danger might stop in the south. Yet the evidence of Stormwind's fall prevailed. Human kingdoms and allied peoples formed the Alliance of Lordaeron, with Lothar commanding its armies. This coalition did not erase its members. It asked them to act together long enough to prevent the fate of one kingdom from becoming the fate of every hall and harbor.

storyNodes.title: The Second War spreads across many roads
storyNodes.narration: Orgrim drove the Horde north against a coalition still learning how to endure. The struggle crossed land and water, threatened several realms, and drew peoples beyond humanity into its widening account. No single line can contain such a war. The route shown is a strategic summary: pressure rising from the conquered south toward the Alliance heartlands, answered by forces whose shared purpose grew under the strain meant to break it.

storyNodes.title: The oldest bargain fractures the Horde
storyNodes.narration: At the height of the northern campaign, Gul'dan withdrew warriors for an ambition that was his alone. The choice exposed what conquest had hidden: the Horde had never been united by one memory or one purpose. Orgrim turned fury upon the deserters, but lost strength and time that could not be recalled. The Alliance survived the pressure, and the offensive began to give way. A betrayal within the invaders opened room for resistance before them.

storyNodes.title: At Blackrock, loss becomes a summons
storyNodes.narration: Near Blackrock Spire, Lothar fell in the struggle with Orgrim. The death of Stormwind's champion might have broken the army he had gathered. Turalyon instead raised the fallen commander's memory before them and called the Alliance forward. Grief became momentum. From that turning, the counteroffensive pressed south—not one perfect march, but a succession of victories carrying the war back toward the threshold through which it had entered.

storyNodes.title: The gate falls, but the road remains in memory
storyNodes.narration: The Alliance drove the Horde back to the Dark Portal and destroyed the original gateway. Many orcs were captured; others remained beyond reach, and Draenor still waited on the far side of a severed road. Victory ended the Second War, not the histories it had entangled. Camps, displaced peoples, wounded kingdoms, and a generation shaped by invasion now stood before the next crisis. From these consequences, the age of the Third War would one day rise.

storyNodes.title: The defeated inherit another beginning
storyNodes.narration: The Second War ended at a broken gate, yet its consequences endured in camps, ruined houses, and children raised beneath another people's watch. From among the interned orcs, Thrall gathered those willing to seek a future unlike the Old Horde's conquest. Liberation did not erase the blood behind them. It opened a harder question: what might a people become when the purpose imposed upon them was no longer their only road?

storyNodes.title: A quiet corruption enters the granaries
storyNodes.narration: While one people broke the locks of an older defeat, Lordaeron trusted in walls, harvests, and the familiar duties of peace. Into that ordered country came a plague whose first victories did not announce themselves with banners. Kel'Thuzad and the Cult of the Damned prepared the way; the Scourge grew where ordinary life had been made its instrument. Arthas and Jaina rode into a crisis whose true command still lay beyond their sight.

storyNodes.title: At Stratholme, purpose hardens into ruin
storyNodes.narration: At Stratholme, fear of what the infected might become narrowed Arthas's answer until no mercy remained within it. He ordered the city purged. Jaina and Uther would not follow that road, and the prince passed onward without them. The city stands here as an approximate light upon the atlas, for the deeper boundary crossed that day was not a city wall. It lay within the man who believed every cost could be justified by pursuit.

storyNodes.title: The hunter follows winter into the north
storyNodes.narration: Arthas carried his pursuit over the cold sea to Northrend. The route shown is only the shape of obsession across the world, not a chart of every landing and march. There he claimed Frostmourne, seeking the strength to defeat the enemy before him. The blade answered that desire by binding him to a greater enemy's will. He had ridden north to save Lordaeron; the man who turned homeward would become the kingdom's destroyer.

storyNodes.title: The prince returns beneath a colder allegiance
storyNodes.narration: The gates of Lordaeron opened to a returning prince and received a servant of the Lich King. Arthas killed his father, and the Scourge passed through the old kingdom's heart. A realm that had survived the Horde's northern war fell through the son it had trusted to defend it. The advance drawn across the map is broad and interpretive, because the catastrophe was larger than one army line: government, memory, and the safety of the living all gave way together.

storyNodes.title: The northern light is broken
storyNodes.narration: The Scourge turned next upon Quel'Thalas. Sylvanas resisted the advance and was answered with a captivity beyond death. The kingdom was broken, and the Sunwell corrupted as the invaders pursued a design reaching farther still. This passage must hold two truths together: a people suffered devastation, and one defender's transformation would later help create a power the Scourge could not wholly command. Ruin had begun to divide even the army of the dead.

storyNodes.title: The hand behind the dead steps through
storyNodes.narration: The Scourge had not been raised for conquest alone. Through the devastation of the north, the way opened for Archimonde and the Burning Legion to enter Azeroth once more. Kingdoms had been made into preparation; the undead host became the road by which an older enemy returned. Yet the Legion's victory in the east did not complete its purpose. Far across the sea stood Kalimdor, Mount Hyjal, and Nordrassil—the next height toward which the invasion bent.

storyNodes.title: A warning sends the New Horde beyond the sunset
storyNodes.narration: Warned that a greater darkness was coming, Thrall led the New Horde westward. The sea passage shown here is a narrative direction, not a captain's measured chart. Across it moved a people seeking ground on which a different future might stand, even while old violence traveled within them. Kalimdor offered no empty refuge. It held ancient guardians, unfamiliar powers, and conflicts that would test whether the new name could survive the habits of the old.

storyNodes.title: The old corruption demands one final answer
storyNodes.narration: Mannoroth's shadow still reached into orcish history. Grom fell again beneath that power, then stood with Thrall against the pit lord who embodied it. He died in the blow that broke the immediate demonic bond over their people. Liberation did not make the past harmless, nor did sacrifice settle every debt. It did remove one chain at the hour when the New Horde would need to choose whether it could stand beside others against the master that chain had served.

storyNodes.title: Three histories gather beneath one mountain
storyNodes.narration: Night elves, New Horde forces, and Alliance survivors did not arrive at Hyjal emptied of suspicion. Each carried losses, loyalties, and reasons to mistrust the others. The Legion gave them a danger none could outlast alone. Their coalition was temporary, and the atlas names it as such. Its meaning lies not in pretending difference vanished, but in showing that distinct peoples accepted one defense when the survival of every road behind them depended upon the mountain ahead.

storyNodes.title: At the World Tree, time becomes the defenders' weapon
storyNodes.narration: The defense yielded ground in order to purchase time. Archimonde climbed toward Nordrassil, believing the height already won. Then Malfurion called upon the power gathered around the World Tree, and the Legion commander was destroyed. The mountain survived, but victory was no return to the morning before the plague. Lordaeron and Quel'Thalas remained broken, the alliance at Hyjal would not become a single people, and the long-lived kaldorei paid a consequence of their own.

storyNodes.title: In fallen Lordaeron, the dead claim their own will
storyNodes.narration: Archimonde's defeat changed the balance far from Hyjal. As the Lich King's control weakened, Sylvanas and other undead broke free and made a place among Lordaeron's ruins. They named themselves the Forsaken. Freedom did not restore their lives or make the broken kingdom whole. It created another claimant to its future—born from the Scourge's cruelty, opposed to its mastery, and destined to complicate every simple division between the living and the dead.

storyNodes.title: Exile crosses into a world already broken
storyNodes.narration: Illidan's path led beyond Azeroth into Outland, where every horizon bore the memory of Draenor's ruin. With Kael'thas, Lady Vashj, and their followers, he closed portals and overthrew Magtheridon's rule. This was not the founding of a peaceful realm. It was the making of a stronghold by an uneasy coalition, shown within Outland's own local atlas. No line joins it falsely to Azeroth; the change of worlds is a change of map and measure.

storyNodes.title: Two purposes narrow toward the throne
storyNodes.narration: From Outland the story returns to Azeroth without pretending the worlds share one road. Illidan came to destroy the Frozen Throne; Arthas hastened north to preserve the power that had claimed him. Around Icecrown, the long histories of plague, exile, and demonic command drew into one contest. The route is a compact diagram of convergence, not a reconstruction of every campaign path. At its end, Illidan fell before he could reach the throne.

storyNodes.title: The lost prince ascends into a colder age
storyNodes.narration: Arthas climbed the Frozen Throne and joined his fate to the Lich King's power. The prince who had pursued the plague in hope of saving Lordaeron now ruled from the winter above the world he helped to break. Yet history did not end beneath that crown. The New Horde, the Forsaken, the survivors of kingdoms, and the peoples joined at Hyjal all carried changed inheritances forward. Beyond this threshold begins the age when adventurers would enter those wounds themselves.

storyNodes.title: The empire stands beneath its last unbroken sky
storyNodes.narration: Ancient Kalimdor entered this age beneath the splendor of the kaldorei empire. Roads and cities answered to Queen Azshara, and the Well of Eternity shone beside her capital like a promise without limit. Few could see that the same concentration of power which made the court magnificent had also made the whole world vulnerable to one circle's choice.

storyNodes.title: A chosen circle turns the Well into a door
storyNodes.narration: Azshara's favored Highborne drew ever more deeply upon the Well. Their work ceased to be only the art of their own civilization: it became a doorway offered to a power beyond the world. The decision belonged to a privileged court, but every forest, city, and people of Kalimdor would be made to bear its consequence.

storyNodes.title: Beyond the gate waits a will vast as ruin
storyNodes.narration: The force answering the Highborne was the Burning Legion, and beyond its first hosts stood Sargeras. The portal was meant to become wide enough for that fallen titan to enter Azeroth. He never stood upon this ground; the figure shown here belongs to the threshold, a warning of the presence the ritual sought to make real.

storyNodes.title: The invasion enters through the heart of empire
storyNodes.narration: Demonic hosts came through Zin-Azshari, and the bright center of the empire became the source of its burning. The Legion's destruction spread beyond any single road or battlefield. This wartime map therefore shows pressure and devastation in broad form, not a false wall of exact fronts across a continent whose campaigns are imperfectly measured.

storyNodes.title: A divided people chooses resistance
storyNodes.narration: Not all kaldorei followed the queen into catastrophe. Soldiers, priests, common defenders, and those who had questioned the court gathered against enemies both foreign and familiar. Their coalition was never one unchanging host. It grew while cities fell, drew strength from many kinds of loyalty, and learned that preserving the world might require opposing the order that had ruled it.

storyNodes.title: Three paths meet within one desperate war
storyNodes.narration: Malfurion listened for powers older than the court. Tyrande carried devotion into the struggle and held others together beneath fear. Illidan trusted dangerous knowledge and his own fierce judgment. Their purposes crossed, parted, and crossed again. None of them alone was the resistance, yet each choice would outlive the world in which it was made.

storyNodes.title: The living world answers the invaders
storyNodes.narration: The war could no longer be contained within kaldorei politics. Cenarius and other ancient powers joined the defense of the land itself, and the dragons entered the struggle from the sky. For a brief hour, beings divided by nature and history acted upon one truth: if the Legion prevailed, there would be no separate refuge left to guard.

storyNodes.title: The weapon of many answers to one will
storyNodes.narration: The Dragon Aspects gave their strength to an artifact meant to break the Legion's advance. Neltharion wielded it, then turned its power upon those who had trusted him. The betrayal wounded the alliance at the moment of greatest need. Victory could no longer depend upon one perfect weapon or upon the unity of the dragons.

storyNodes.title: The war returns to the water at its beginning
storyNodes.narration: Every surviving purpose narrowed again toward the Well. The defenders reached the gateway before Sargeras could cross, and the ritual was broken. Yet the portal had been joined too deeply to the power beneath it. Stopping the invasion did not restore the old world. It set loose a collapse no army, queen, dragon, or demigod could command.

storyNodes.title: One continent becomes a memory
storyNodes.narration: The Well collapsed. Seas rushed into the wound, the old land broke, and distances that had been crossed by road became oceans. At the center remained the Maelstrom, turning above the place where power and pride had drawn ruin together. This is a separate world state, not an ornament laid over the old one: ancient Kalimdor was gone.

storyNodes.title: The sea closes over the queen's old world
storyNodes.narration: Azshara and Highborne followers were taken beneath the waters, yet the depths did not end their history. They survived through transformation, while the cities that had proclaimed their permanence vanished below the new sea. The tour marks this fate without placing an exact underwater court upon a map whose drowned geography remains uncertain.

storyNodes.title: Survivors carry the old world toward Hyjal
storyNodes.narration: Across broken shores, many survivors came at last toward Mount Hyjal. They brought grief, memory, old divisions, and powers that the war had not resolved. The map's single route is only a broad direction, for they did not all travel as one company. Here the age of invasion ends, and the long keeping of the sundered world begins.
